chunks.h: Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks
chunks.x: The Klobase framework calls lifecycle hook methods on your controller class at specific points in the page's life. Understanding WHEN each fires is essential — using the wrong hook causes bugs that are hard to trace because they appear intermittently depending on navigation order.

chunks.h: Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks > B.1 — Hook Execution Order
chunks.x:
On first page load: onPageInit → onPageModelReady → onPageEnter

On forward navigation back to same page: onPageEnter (only)

On backward navigation away from page: onPageExit (source page), onPageEnter (target page)

On back-navigation that destroys the page: onPageExit → onPageDestroy

| Hook | When It Fires | Model Data Available? | Primary Use Cases | Common Mistakes |

chunks.h: Part B — Controller Page Lifecycle Hooks > B.2 — Lifecycle Hook Reference
chunks.x:
| onPageInit | Once, when controller class loads. UI, model, and TransNodes do NOT exist yet. | No | Rare: one-time non-model setup like subscribing to a global service. | Trying to access this.tm or TransNodes — they are null at this point. |
| onPageModelReady | Once (per page lifecycle), after TransNodes are initialized but BEFORE data is fetched. | No (TransNodes exist but have no data) | Call this.tm.getTN('search').skipModelPreparation() to skip auto-query execution and manually control data load. | Reading TransNode data — getData() returns null or empty. The fetch hasn't happened yet. |
| onPageEnter | Every time the page becomes visible — forward nav, backward nav, and initial load. | Yes | Dashboard count calculations. Resetting UI state. Refreshing summaries. Setting default filter values. | Putting logic that should only run ONCE here — it re-runs on every navigation. Use _initialized flag for one-time logic. |
| onPageExit | When the user navigates AWAY to a different page. | Yes | Auto-save draft, log exit event, clear unsaved state. | Not called for within-page section navigation (SS). Only fires on cross-page navigation. |
| onPageDestroy | Once, when the page is removed from memory (back-nav that exits the page history). | Partially | Unsubscribe event listeners. Release resources. Not needed for most standard screens. | Using it as a reliable 'save on exit' hook — the page may be destroyed without user navigation (memory pressure, app backgrounding). |

These standards are non-negotiable on all Procify projects. Violations result in code review rejection and technical debt. The principles come from kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide §7.4 and §7.5.

| Rule | Do | Don't | Reason |

chunks.h: Part E — Coding Standards > E.1 — Controller File Standards
chunks.x:
| Scope | Write ONLY UI logic in the controller: formatters, navigation, show/hide, model reads for display. | Write business logic (status transitions, validations, default-setting) in the controller. | Business logic in the controller bypasses server validation and breaks when the screen is accessed via API. |
| TypeScript typing | Declare every variable with its type: const count: number \= 0; const msg: string \= ''; | Use implicit any: let x \= someValue; or omit types on function parameters. | Untyped code hides bugs at compile time that surface as runtime errors in production. |
| Variable declaration | Declare variables only when necessary. Prefer const over let. | Declare variables at file scope (class properties) when a local variable suffices. | File-scope variables persist across page navigations and cause state leakage between sessions. |
| Nested functions | Keep functions flat. Extract complex logic to named private methods. | Nest arrow functions inside controller methods: onClick(() \=> { const x \= () \=> {...}; }) | Nested functions are not testable, not readable, and difficult to debug. |
| Async/await | Use async/await for all TransNode API calls. Mark the function async. | Use .then().catch() promise chains. | Consistent await pattern is required by the framework for proper error propagation. |
| Deprecated APIs | Always use navTo(), tm.commitP(), this.setMode(). | Use navToS(), navToByEvent(), getTN('x').commitP() | Deprecated APIs are removed in future versions. Using them creates upgrade risk. |
| Model mutation | Only modify model properties via setProperty() for transient display values. | Directly mutate entity properties from the controller (entity.some_prop \= value). | Direct mutations bypass the dirty-tracking mechanism and do not persist on save. |

chunks.h: Part E — Coding Standards > E.2 — Entity File Standards
chunks.x:
| Rule | Do | Don't |

| Scope | Write ONLY business logic in entity files: onCreate defaults, onUpdate role checks, onDelete restrictions, beforeQ filtering, OnValidate. | Write navigation or UI state changes in entity files. |
| Setter functions | Use setter override pattern to automatically derive related values when a property changes. | Compute derived values in the controller on button press — this is bypassed when data changes via API. |
| Validation location | All mandatory field checks and business rule violations go in OnValidate. | Throw errors in onAfterCreate — onAfterCreate is called AFTER the record is saved; errors there cause data inconsistency. |
| Error handling | Always wrap async BOL API calls (createEntityP, LoadEntityByKeyP) in try/catch and log errors. | Let unhandled promise rejections propagate silently. |
| Role checks in rules | Use oEvent.getTxn().\$SYSTEM.roleID to get the runtime role and enforce role-specific logic. | Hardcode user IDs or email addresses for role checks. |

chunks.h: Part C — App Status Lifecycle & Versioning > C.1 — App Status Values
chunks.x:
Every version of an application on the Procify platform has a Status that controls what operations are allowed on it. Understanding these statuses is essential before releasing or transporting.

| Status | Meaning | Can Develop? | Can Transport? | Can Create New Version? |

| ACTIVE | Current working version. All development happens here. | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| RELEASED | Development complete and locked. Ready for transport. | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (create from RELEASED) |
| DEPRECATED | Retired. Superseded by a newer version. | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| DISCARDED | Abandoned branch/version. Excluded from main path. | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ No |

| ⚠  Important Critical Versioning Rules — memorise these before proceeding A NEW VERSION can only be created from a RELEASED version. A BRANCH can only be created from an ACTIVE version. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Merge the branch into a new version first, then transport. Once status is changed to RELEASED, no further development is possible on that version. Always build (Validate & Publish) BEFORE changing status to RELEASED. |

chunks.h: Part D — App Branching and Merging > D.1 — Why Branch?
chunks.x:
A Branch creates a parallel ACTIVE copy of your application. Use it when you need to work on next-phase enhancements while the current version is being tested in QA. The branch is fully isolated — changes in the branch don't affect the main RELEASED version until you explicitly merge them.

| Scenario | Use Branch? |

| Bug fix on the current version in QA | ❌ No — fix directly in main, create new minor version |
| New feature development while current is in QA | ✅ Yes — branch from current ACTIVE version |
| Experimental UI changes for client review | ✅ Yes — branch lets you show without committing to main |

chunks.h: Part F — Transport: DEV to QA > F.1 — How Transport Works
chunks.x:
Transport is a PULL mechanism: the TARGET system (QA) asks the SOURCE system (DEV) for the latest published version. You perform ALL transport steps while logged into the QA environment, not DEV.

| Stage | What Happens |

| Setup | Transport creates entries in QA metadata tables for the application, groups, and flavors. |
| Download | Application ZIPs are pulled from DEV and extracted in the QA server's file system. |
| Update Schema | Database tables for all entities are created or altered in the QA database. |
| Finalising | Application is set to ACTIVE in QA so users can log in and access it. |

| ⚠  Important Transport Pre-requisites — verify ALL before starting 1. The application must be in RELEASED status on the DEV system. 2. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Create a new version, merge, then transport. 3. The QA server's config.json must have mm_klo_online_server pointing to the DEV landscape URL. 4. A host file entry for the DEV system must exist on the QA server. 5. The transport_1 app must be assigned to the developer account on the QA system. If any pre-requisite is missing, the transport will fail at Setup or Download stage. Ask the trainer to verify the QA environment config before proceeding. |

**ClientGlobalObj** of the ClientGlobal class of **ADM clients** is available globally to be used by application developers. It provides the following variables and methods which help application developers to configure different aspects of client features.

**ADM client registration log** details are also explained in this document.

**Variables are recommended for changes in the index.html page after rendering of ClientGlobal class. For example, suppose the variable name is a system so in index.html it is changed as clientGlobalObj.system = “KLARION”**

**clientGlobalObj.system = "KLARION";**

1.  **system** - Used to specify the system in which an application is running. Currently, there are only two values that can be used i.e. KLARION or SAP. By default the system value is Klarion.

> **public system: "KLARION" | "SAP" = 'KLARION';**

2.  **deviceType** - Used to specify the device in which the application is running. Values are browser or cordova. Currently, its value is maintained automatically depending on the device type i,e if the device is a browser then the value is a browser and if it is cordova (Mobile) then its value is cordova.

> **public deviceType: "Cordova" | "Browser";**

3.  **sapUITheme** - Used to set sap UI library themes. The default value is **sap_belize_plus**

> **public sapUITheme: string = "sap_belize_plus";**

4.  **sapUIVersion** - Used to set the sap UI library version. The default value is **1.102.7**

> **public sapUIVersion:string = "1.102.7"**

5.  **appName -** Used to specify the name of the application. It is used to construct url SAP related URLs for seam4 type of application

> Eg: moast4, seam4 etc.

6.  **baseRot** - List of rot/app/flavor which can be mentioned at the beginning in index.html, which will be downloaded and extracted before the registration page is visible.

> **Note**: - Until the baseRot is downloaded, the user cannot perform any kind of operation. Treat it as a mandatory rot/app/flavor which is required before the user can perform any operation
>
> **Structure of list: [{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildNo:number}]**
>
> **public baseRot:Array\ = [];**

7.  **extendedRot -** List of rot/app / flavortotally similar to baseRot with only one difference: it will get downloaded and extracted in the background. I.e User will not have to wait to begin any operation.

> **Structure of list: [{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildNo:number}]**
>
> **public extendedRot:Array\ = [];**

8.  **documentTitle -** Used to specify title value in the title tag of html page. For more information refer to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/title

9.  **isLog** - Boolean value to enable or disable clientGlobalObject log. The log can be accessed using clientGlobalObject._log

10. **preloadScript** - List of script files with the proper path which can be mentioned in the index.html file which will get loaded in the client before the user can perform any operation.

> Eg:
>
> **clientGlobalObj.preloadScript=["closedmodules/kloExternal/core.js"]**

11. **postLoadScript** - List of script files with a proper path similar to preloadScript with only one difference. Users do not have to wait for the script to load to perform any operation.

12. **enableBioMetric** - its value is either true or false based on that you will view a biometric login at the offline login page. By default true is maintained

13. **is_browser_sync** - value is either true or false. If true then the middleware works through the index DB of the client and if the value is false or not maintained then the middleware works through the sync **adapter**.

14. **oUIConfig** - It is an object containing a key-value pair which is used to hide or show a particular view/div in the index.html page.

**Note:** Developers can add more key value in this object for their usage.

> Key value pair listed below:
>
>

**The below methods are for developers.**

**All methods take two parameters, the first parameter is the definition of the callback method and the second parameter is the context of the class where that callback method is defined.**

**Eg: clientGlobalObj.attachShowError(this._fnShowErrorPage,this);**

Here **fnShowErrorPage** is the method definition you want to attach to an attachShowError method and this is class context or class ‘this’ where fnShowErrorPage is defined

1.  **attachShowError( errFn , context )**

Attach your error page to what you want to display in the UI when any error comes. Framework will internally call this method when any error comes.

2.  **attachLoadComponent(loadComponentFn,context)**

Attach your component method using this function. Components can be seam4 components or any other SAP component. By default, the framework uses the kloTouch component to load after registration.

3.  **attachOfflinePageLockMethod(offlinePageLockFn,context)**

Attach your offline lock method which will be called during offline login by the framework.

4.  **attachForgetPasswordOffline(offlineForgetPasswordFn,context)**

Attach your offline forget password UI method by calling the upper method which will be internally called by the framework to display the offline forget password page.

5.  **clientGlobalObj.htmlBanner.showHTMLUpgradeBanner(actionButtonEventHandler,targetContainerId,message?:string,actionButtonText?,timeLimitInMinutes?:number, timerLimitInTimestamp?)**

Attach your html banner on the top level of the page by calling the upper method.

**5.1. Parameters -**

- **actionButtonEventHandler (mandatory)** - A reference to the function that will be called when the user clicks on the action button present in the banner or after the specified time passes.

- **targetContainerId (mandatory)** - This will take the html container id. To use the banner similar to the upgrade banner, provide “html_banner_container” as the value.

- **Message (optional)-** This will take the message to be displayed in the banner. By default it takes the hardcoded Upgrade message.

- **actionButtonText (optional)-** This will take the text to be displayed in the action button. By default it takes hardcoded text ”Upgrade Now”.

- **timeLimitInMinutes (optional)-** This will take the time for which the banner will be displayed. Value must be in minutes, once the time limit is expired/once the user is clicking on the action button, the actionButtonEventHandler will be called automatically. By default, it is set to 3 minutes.

- **timerLimitInTimestamp (optional)-** This is the same as the above time limit, it can be passed in timestamp.

**6.clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() -** It removes data from Local Storage, Session Storage, and any cached data. After the data is cleared, the page will reload, and the user will be redirected to the registration page. For devices with QR functionality enabled, the user will be directed to the QR scanner page.

> **Note: It is recommended to use this API only when necessary, as it may result in data loss.**

To view the registration log, open the browser console and type clientGlobalObj._log. **Note:** The data in this variable will be cleared if the page is refreshed or the app is reopened.

It has several levels like initial sync, tablegeneraton etc. It will show the time of start and time of the end of any process and if any error occurs it will log that error. In the account console all the childline items logs can be accessed.

chunks.h: From Console > Detailing about the Childline item
chunks.x:
- **"Initial sync"** refers to the process of syncing data from the server to the client. When a user registers, all their relevant data is transferred from the server and stored in the client’s local database, enabling the application to function offline.

- The term **"DeviceRegisterCall"** refers to the registration process of a user in a system and after this assigned flavors can be fetched for the user.

- **ST** here, stands for **Start Time**, which indicates the starting timestamp of an activity/process.

- **ET** here stands for **End Time**, which indicates the ending timestamp of an activity/process.
  > Here, **ST and ET** is stored to track how much time an activity is taking to complete.

- **noofqueries**: The total number of SQL queries that has been executed during the initialSync process of a particular flavor.

- **noofsqlrecords**: The total number of data/ records that have already been fetched after executing the queries.

> Eg:In this case;(shown in above screenshot)
>
> **55 SQL queries** were executed.
>
> A total of **1324 records** data were retrieved.

chunks.h: From Console > Detailing about the Childline item
chunks.x:
- **"queryids"** typically refers to unique identifiers associated with individual SQL queries or database queries that are executed by a system. Each **queryid** helps track, identify, or differentiate between specific queries that are run, making it easier to debug, analyze performance, or monitor system behavior. This contains the ids of all the initial sync queries in that particular application.

- **“ROTdownload”** stands for root download. It contains the list of applications’ zips that have been downloaded.

- **“table generator”** for storing above data in the client side tables corresponding table are required. In clientGlobalObj._log is generating table logs on the client side in opfs/ sqlite db/ etc.

- **“Before Login”,** track user input, validation, and any checks made before the user is authenticated.

- **“After Login”,** track session creation, successful login, and post-login actions.

- **“TT”** often refers to **Total Time**. This is the amount of time it takes to complete a particular activity or query in a system.

> **Note**:Similar for every flavor as shown in the below screenshots there are activity log details of ET,noofqueries,noofsqlrecords,STATUS,Queryids,ST,and TT.

For the app setup, any failures during the setup process (including config updates) will be displayed in the about page. Icons are used to indicate the setup status: a green icon represents success, while a red icon indicates failure.This approach provides a user-friendly and informative method for handling only the **InitialSync** setup issues.

Clicking on the red icon opens a popup that shows any associated error messages. From the popup, users can download the logs in a .txt file format by clicking the **Download Log** button, or they can reinstall the app by selecting the **Reinstall** button.

The **"Download Log"** option typically refers to the ability to download a record or history of events or actions taken within a specific application or system. This log file might contain useful information such as:

- System actions or operations performed

- Errors or warnings encountered

- timestamps

The purpose of downloading the log is usually for record-keeping for understanding the system's performance. The format of the log file can be downloaded in **txt** format using the download log button present in the popup.

App Mover is a standalone application resource.

**Step 1:** In the portal’s menu tab, go to **Admin Center**.

**Step 2:** Under Admin Center select **Advanced Migration**. You will be taken to the installation screen.

A preview of the Installation Screen is given below:

The installation screen is used to install or update external apps. This includes the app’s folder that will be saved in the closedmodules folder and its zip will be extracted in cdn_app. Apart from this, the installation screen does the following tasks in the background:

- Update **madm_app** table.

- Update the Flavor folder in the closedmodules folder.

- Update the Flavor zip in the **cdn_app** folder.

- Create/Update Tables for that App and its dependent app.

- Install Config for that App.

The screen will have a table which contains all information relevant to the app.

Following is a list of columns in the app installation screen like the App name.

| **Components**    | **Description**                                                                                                                                         |

| **App**           | Name of the app.                                                                                                                                        |
| **BOL Version**   | BOL version used by the app.                                                                                                                            |
| **Version**       | A version of the app.                                                                                                                                   |
| **Is External**   | It is a component of the app. If **is_external** is marked as false then the app is in closedmodules, if marked as true then the app is in **cdn_app**. |
| **Dependant App** | Shows the dependent app information of a particular app with the dependent app name and version.                                                        |
| **Created On**    | Shows the date app was created.                                                                                                                         |
| **Landscape**     | The landscape where the apps are present.                                                                                                               |

To install an app follow the following steps:

1.  Click the **Upload App** button on the top left of the screen to select the zip file and press OK.
    > **Note:** zip name should be proper for eg:- **app_version.zip**.

>

2.  Then a popup screen will appear that will give relevant details related to the app, if the app is already there in the **madm_app** table then it will ask for an **install**. If it's not there then it will ask for an **update**.

>

3.  On click of install or update, **madm_app** will be updated, tables for that app will be generated and the app zip will be placed inside closed modules with extracted files.

There is one download button that lets you download any app‘s zip from the current server (**cdn_app**) where the application is running.

>

**Note:-**

- If the app is internal (i.e. r_is_external = 0), it will be downloaded from the cdn_app/release_build folder (i.e. prodBuild zip).

- If the app is external (i.e. r_is_external = 1), it will be downloaded from the cdn_app folder (i.e. devBuild zip).

- Whenever you make any changes in an existing app that has already been moved using the Advanced app mover; You need to change the app version make the changes in the app and then move the app. This will help in triggering the Update Schema through the URL. Application URLs support version-based access using the following format:

https://\/appservice/\/\_\/\

where \ follows the format:

--\

When resolving an application version:

- The specified **major** and **minor** versions are honored.

- The system automatically resolves the request to the latest available patch version within the specified major.minor version.

App Branching is done to create a branch of the actual app. This branch will be helpful in cases where the team wants to work on next-phase developments and at the same time provide fixes for the released application. Developers can create a new branch for the next phase of development and use this for the developments. When the developments are complete, the branch can be merged with the latest version of the app.

To simplify this let's take a look at the below explanation:

In the above diagram, we have an app named **eam_6.0.1**. Now there is a major enhancement that needs to be done for this app. This enhancement might take a long period to develop. This will automatically pause the further development progress of the app.

Therefore, we will create a branch for this app. All the major developments will be done in this branch app. In the meantime, minor fixes and other changes are made to the main app and the versions are updated. Once the enhancement is complete the branch app will be exported along with the latest version and both will be merged into one major app version as the final product.

The Status Change Process is used for segregating the version and branch hierarchy process to identify each dependent app and sequence.

- **From Active, status can be changed to Released, Discarded.**

- **From Released, status can be changed to Deprecated.**

- **Deprecated: No users should be assigned to the App.**

- **Discarded: All the changes in the app will be discarded and not be considered in the main branch.**

- **Only from the Released version, a new version can be created.**

- **Only from Active Version, a new Branch can be created.**

- **Development can be only done in the App with Active Status.**

- **A branch can be ACTIVE, DEPRECATED, or DISCARDED.**

Publish Status Process is used to check if any other app build is in progress / in queue. It helps with sequence and smooth processes.

It checks which apps are **in process** or **in queue** to be **Built** before you proceed with the current app. If you still want to proceed then you can click on the **Proceed** button.

App Cache Settings, as the name suggests, is for developers as a helping tool while developing applications.

Previously, if any offline entity was created, any metadata was updated, or any entry was made in the server-side database, it required developers to clear their cache and do registration again to get it reflected in the browser. To resolve that issue, a App Cache Settings is introduced.

Now, developers can update zip, drop and create web SQL tables, update configs (eg: vh configs), and do initial sync to get server data without any middleware sync (sync of data in the background whenever the device/browser is online).

**Note:** The App Cache Settings should be handled by developers only to avoid any inconsistency or failure in the application.

| Update Config | Update application-related configs. (eg- vh config) |

**App merging** is the process of merging one application branch with the current main branch (or vice versa) or merging one active branch into another active branch. It is important to note that this process merges **metadata only.**

- **Need to assign cockpit and account flavors**

- **Developer access is required to work on the targeted flavor.**

- **Deployment of the app/flavor should occur within a development environment**.

- **If you're merging into the main version, the main version must be active; if merging into a branch version, then the branch must be active.**

**For Example:** From version 1.0.2 of our app, we created a new branch, 1.0B.2, for developing a new feature. While the feature is being developed, changes may still occur in the main branch. Once the new feature is completed, we need to merge it back into the main branch.

| **Version Type**        | **Description**                                         | **Example** |

| **Base Version**        | The starting version from which the branch was created. | **1.0.2**   |
| **Latest Main Version** | The most recent, stable version of the main branch.     | **1.0.5**   |
| **Branch Version**      | The version where the new feature has been developed.   | **1.0B.2**  |

For the application merge, we need to consider three versions of the application:

1.  **Target Version**

2.  **Source Version**

3.  **Base Version**

The **Target Version** is where the changes will be applied after the merge. It is **pre-filled by default** based on where the user initiated the merge from.

- If the user navigates from a **Branch**, then that branch is the Target.

- If the user navigates from a **Latest Main Version**, then that main version is the Target.

| **User Navigated From** | **Target Version** |

| A **Branch**            | That Branch        |
| A **Main Version**      | That Main Version  |

The **Source Version** is selected by the user from a dropdown. The dropdown options depend on the type of Target:

| **Target Type**  | **Source Options**                          |

| **Branch**       | **Main Released Versions, Active Branches** |
| **Main Version** | Only **Branches** of the App                |

The **Base Version** is **automatically determined** based on the selected Source and Target. It represents the **common ancestor** between the two — the point from which both versions diverged.

You want to compare how **both the Source and Target** have changed **since they split from the same origin** — that's the **Base**.

Usually, the Base Version is the version from which:

- The **Branch was created**, or

- The **Main Version was forked** for changes.

| **Scenario** | **Base Version Logic** |

| **Branch → Main** 🔄
**Main → Branch** | The version from which the Branch was created
The version from which the Branch was created |
| **Branch → Branch** | The most recent common version in both branch sequences |

If there is any altered content in both the **Latest Main Version** and the **Branch Version**, it will be considered a conflict and must be resolved by the developer (user).

The user will be presented with a selection option to choose either the Main Version or the Branch Version for the merge. Any further modifications can be made after the merge is imported into the version if needed.

The conflicts should be resolved by the user based on their selection and any required adjustments as shown below;

**Example:
** To illustrate the merge concepts discussed above, let's consider a simple scenario.

**Case 1: Auto-Merge
** The title on our screen is **"App Console"**. In the **Branch Version**, we are updating the title to **"Workspace Hub"**.

**Case 2: Auto-Merge
**The title on our screen is **"App Console"**. In the **Main Branch Version,** we are changing the title to **"Workspace Hub".**

During the merge, the changes will be compared with the three sets, and it will be determined that the update is only in the **Main Branch Version.** Since this is an update exclusive to the Main Branch, it will be auto-merged into the branch without any conflicts.

**Case 3: Conflict
** The title on our screen is **"App Console"**.

- In the **Branch Version**, we are changing the title to **"Workspace Hub"**.

- In the **Main Version**, we are changing the title to **"Account Cockpit"**.

During the merge, the changes will be compared across the three sets. It will be determined that there are changes in both the **Branch Version** and the **Main Version** when compared to the **Base Version**. This results in a **conflict**, as both versions have different updates to the title.

The user will need to manually resolve this conflict by selecting the appropriate title or making adjustments as needed.

| **Aspect** | **Details** |

| **Merge Target** | Only the **active version** (Main or Branch) can receive merged changes. |
| **Merge Concurrency** | Only **one branch merge at a time** is allowed. No support for simultaneous merges. |
| **Automatic Merge Scope** | Only **metadata** merges are handled automatically. |
| **Manual Merge Required** | **Files** like controllers, entities, queries, utils, resources require **manual intervention**. |
| **Unchanged Items** | No changes are applied if items are identical across all three versions (Base, Branch, Main). |
| **Auto-Merge Conditions** | Change exists **only in Branch Version** → Auto-merge
Change exists **only in Latest Main Version** → Auto-merge |
| **Conflict Handling** | - If conflicts exist, they must be resolved **manually** by the user.
- Compare **Branch vs Base** and **Main vs Base** to identify differences.
- Then compare the resulting changes for **conflicts**. |
| **Default Target** | The **Target App Version** is pre-filled based on the version/branch the user navigated from. |
| **Source Options Based on Target Type** | If Target is a **Branch**, Source dropdown lists Released **Main versions** and **Active Branches**.
If Target is a **Main version**, Source dropdown lists only **Branches**. |
| **Base Version Selection** | **Automatically determined** based on Source and Target versions. |
| **Supported Merge Directions** | ✅ Branch → Main
✅ Main → Branch
✅ Branch → Branch |

- Manually resolve conflicts by choosing one version, merging changes, or customizing a final output

**Example**: If both versions have updated the entity_property_name field differently, you can decide which version to keep or manually edit the final result.

chunks.h: 1.7. FAQs > ❓:What happens if the build fails or the page is refreshed during the process?
chunks.x:
**A**:If the build fails or the user refreshes the screen, the process will resume from the build stage, not from the merge stage.

Similarly, if the first two stages (e.g., schema validation and merge) are completed during the merge process but the process is interrupted midway, the system will resume from the update schema stage, not from the beginning.

chunks.h: 1.7. FAQs > ❓:What happens if there is a conflict during the process?
chunks.x:
**A:**If there is a conflict — such as an app merge issue or a failure in two processes — a conflict screen will appear. This screen allows the user to resolve the conflicts before continuing with the merge.

Additionally, if config data is present in the flavor, and the buildconfig, or any other process fails, the conflict screen will also appear to let the user address the issue before proceeding.

chunks.h: 1.7. FAQs > ❓:What happens if the process is interrupted or canceled?
chunks.x:
**A:**If the process is canceled or the screen is refreshed or the browser is changed, or an error occurs, the conflict screen will not reappear if the app merge has already been completed.

In this case, the process will resume from where it left off — except when copying config data. If the interruption happens during the config copy stage, the process will restart from getting the app details.

App overriding is a feature where the child apps inherit the features of the parent app and override their properties. This screen is used to display and highlight the overridden elements and their properties.

This screen can be used for;

1.  To summarize all the overridden elements along with their root elements in a tree hierarchy.

2.  To categorize the overridden elements (based on entity/page/menu etc.).

3.  To display and compare all the properties of the selected element with its parent flavor and other versions of the same flavor.

4.  To represent all the modified versions of the parent and child app and compare their element's properties.

5.  To navigate to the respective element's page.

Maintaining a proper hierarchy between app versions is crucial for accurate dependency management, for this a correct approach to establish a multi-level hierarchy is required, ensuring that dependencies are calculated correctly.

To maintain the hierarchy effectively, it always starts from **the top-most parent** and works your way down to the **bottom-most child.**

**Example**:

**Current Versions:**

- A-1 (Top-most Parent)

- B-1

- C-1

- D-1 (Bottom-most Child)

**Correct Hierarchy:** A-1 -> B-1 -> C-1 -> D-1

**Note**: To ensure accurate dependency management;

- Always maintain hierarchy from the top-most parent to the bottom-most child.

- This method prevents errors in dependency calculations and keeps the app structure coherent.

- App start

- App moves to the foreground

- App goes into the background

- App close

This allows an efficient and organized management of application behavior in response to above mentioned events.

}

onAppForeground
This method is called when the application comes to the foreground from the background. It is useful for resuming tasks and refreshing data.

Transport is a tool that deploys applications from one server to another. It is mainly aimed at deploying from a dev system to QA system and from QA to PROD system but can be used across any system.

Transportation of an application can be from:

- DEV to QA

- QA to PROD

- DEV to DEV

Steps involved:

- DEV to QA

  - **Setup** **-** Doing entries in tables like madm_app, madm_app_grp etc.

  - **Download-** Downloading and extracting application zips from the source.

  - **Update Schema -** Creating tables on the server for entities of that app.

  - **Finalizing -** Making the app ACTIVE so that everyone can use it.

Transport takes care of the following:

- Maintaining entries of applications in tables like madm_app,mf_fl,mf_fv etc., if any.

- Moving application zips across the system (QA or PROD system) and extracting them.

- Getting the metadata of the application from the source DEV system and extracting it in the target DEV system.

- Running automated scripts if maintained.

- Track manual scripts and run when required.

- Publishing Application.

- Doing an updated schema on the application.

Transport works on a pull mechanism where the target system asks for the latest update from the source system. All the below activities needed to be done on the target system.

**NOTE : Branch flavors cannot be transported or moved to any system. For doing so, create a new version, merge that branch to the new version and then move the new version to any system.**

When you install an app in a DEV landscape, App transport asks whether to install it **As Readable** or **As Writable**. The choice decides what is copied to the target landscape and what you can change there afterward.

|                                             | **As Readable (Read-Only)**                                 | **As Writable**                                       |

| **What is moved**                           | The built application package (zip) only                    | The app’s full metadata from the source DEV landscape |
| **Can the app be developed in the target?** | No                                                          | Yes                                                   |
| **Can App Dependencies be maintained?**     | No (see below)                                              | Yes                                                   |
| **Typical use**                             | Consuming an app as-is, e.g., in QA/PROD or as a parent app | Continuing development in another DEV landscape       |

**Why App Dependencies can’t be maintained for a Read-Only app**

A Read-Only app has no metadata in the target landscape. It only has its built package. Maintaining App Dependencies writes a generated sequence to the database, and the app must be built again afterward. A Read-Only app can’t be built in the target landscape, so its dependencies can’t be changed there.

*Example:* VP depends on OHR (VP ← OHR). If the dependency configuration has to change on the OHR side, OHR must be installed **As Writable**. Alternatively, make the change in the source landscape and migrate it again.

**Note:** If you might need to change an app’s dependencies in the target landscape, install it **As Writable**. **[Confirm]** Whether a Read-Only app can be switched to Writable later, or must be reinstalled.

chunks.t: When should you use the build process?
chunks.x:
The build process is not needed every time; it should only be used in specific scenarios. Below are the cases when you should use the build:

1.  Under prodBuild, whenever the developer needs to deploy apps to the QA server, a build is required.

2.  After entity creation, whenever we change the persists on of the entity,build is required.

3.  Whenever we maintain the Parent -child hierarchy, we need to build.

4.  Whenever we are creating vh-config, we need to build.

5.  Before doing import/export of apps, you need to build.

6.  Whenever you create new version of app, we need to build (this build is done automatically by the account console)

7.  For mobile apps, whenever you want to test app changes, you need to build.

8.  For both devBuild and prodBuild, if we are creating new env roles then we need to build.

Note:

1.  When the fw_version of the application is changed, a new flavor_build must be created and re-registration will be required.

2.  The build process (both devBuild and prodBuild) should follow a parent → child order. You can trigger builds for both flavors at once. However, if the devBuild or prodBuild of a parent flavor has not been completed before building its child flavor, you will encounter an error like this:Error: **Parent app(s) parent_app must be dev/prodbuilt before building child_app**.

When creating a build URL, the current klobase version (known as bol_version) must be included for the **core_fw** component. The bol_version indicates the version of the build running on the system and should be included in the URL to generate the correct build.

Suppose the current **bol_version** running in the system is **7-2-27.**

Before adopting the **current_bol_version,** the build URL would look like this:

https://dev.procifynow.com/node/EAM/core_fw_6-0/generateBuild?fv=my_test_6-0-1&buildtype=

After updating to the current **bol_version (7-2-27),** the build URL format will be updated as follows:

https://dev.procifynow.com/node/\/core_fw_\/generateBuild?fv=\_\&buildtype=\

For the example provided with a **current_bol_version** of **7-2-27**, the updated URL would look like this:

https://dev.procifynow.com/node/EAM/core_fw_7-2-27/generateBuild?fv=my_test_6-0-1&buildtype=devbuild

**Note:
** To generate a build URL for the core_fw version:

1.  Retrieve the current bol_version from the system using clientGlobalObj._bolVersion.

2.  Update the URL with the correct core_fw version and the appropriate build type.

3.  Use the following format:
    > https://dev.procifynow.com/node/\/core_fw_\/generateBuild?fv=\_\&buildtype=\
    > This ensures the build URL points to the correct version and build type for the system.

This depicts the domain name for which the build needs to be executed.

**Examples:** demo.com, aws.demo.com, maven.com, dev.procify.com, testing.procify.com

**Format:**

*\_\ (**underscore** between flavor and version)*

Parameter values can be **allFlavor** or any individual flavor name or multiple flavors separated by a comma.

| **Parameter Values** | **Functionality**                                                                                                    |

| allFlavor            | This will build all the flavors maintained in the flavor master table, excluding **account** and **core_fw flavor**. |

build_type also known as task_type defines the behavior of flavor build. The build type defines the type of build being generated. The available options are below in the list ;

| **Build type** | **Functionality**                                                                                                          |

| devBuild       | Build files will be unminified i.e., the codes and script files are not minimized.                                         |
| prodBuild      | Build files will be minified i.e., minimizing code and script files.                                                       |
| checkStatus    | It will check the status of the current build process.(can also be used with an empty string to return the current status) |
| cancelPending  | It will terminate the build process, if multiple flavors are in the queue it will remove those flavors from the queue.     |
| applyChange    | It will identify duplicates, and inconsistencies in the metadata and align them.                                           |

**Note:** The default value of buildtype is **checkStatus**.

It provides all the dependent flavors' names and details for the specified flavor.

Supported values : 0 / 1

When the value is 1, the mentioned fv’s dependent flavors will be built. If the value is 0 it will not include the dependent flavors.

**Step 1 - Trigger Build URL**

Trigger the build URL in the browser.

**URL:**

https://maven63.com/node/mytrunk/core_fw_6-0/generateBuild?fv=eam_1&buildtype=devBuild

Provide the user credentials and click on sign in.

Once triggered it will show you the flavor that is being used, the time, the task type, the status version, etc. The status will be **IN_PROCESS**.

If Status is

- **In Queue**: This status indicates that your build request is waiting to be processed. The reason for the delay could be that another flavor build is currently being processed on the server. Once the server finishes the other build, your build will be processed next.

- **In Process**: This status means that your flavor build is currently being processed on the server. It’s in progress, and the system is actively working on your build.

- **Completed**: This status signifies that your flavor build has been successfully completed. At this point, you can proceed with further actions or processes related to this build.

*A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.*

**Every Application / App version built on the Procify platform uses a FW/Platform version. The platform releases a new version every month with new features and bug fixes reported. It is recommended for users to stay updated with the latest version of the platform.**

**This document serves as a guide for users on the understanding of Framework version updation(upgrade/downgrade) for applications. If an app running on the latest Framework version requires adjustments, users can use this guide to revert to an earlier version. This process involves either upgrading or downgrading the FW version.**

**Note:Framework version can be changed only for ACTIVE Apps.**

**App FW version cannot be changed by users when it's in QA/production.**

chunks.t: When to create a new app version?
chunks.x: New version creation is recommended while giving any major/minor fixes or any new changes happening in the FW version. So whenever there is any update in the FW, then the application which uses this older framework version has to be updated to ensure optimal performance.

chunks.t: Framework Downgrade Scenarios in the Application
chunks.x:
Our application is designed to operate with a specific Framework (FW) version. However, in certain situations, it may be necessary to downgrade the FW version to maintain compatibility, stability, or consistency across different environments. Below are the scenarios where a FW downgrade is required:

1.  **Latest FW Version Unavailable in QA and Production Environments
    > ** **Scenario:** The latest FW version is deployed only in the development environment, but it has not been made available in the QA or production environments.
    > **Reason for Downgrade:
    > **

    - To ensure that the application team can move their developments to QA and production environments without facing compatibility issues.

    - To align the development environment with the FW version currently in use in the QA and production environments.

2.  **Limited Testing of the Application with the Latest FW Version
    > ** **Scenario:** The application has only been partially tested with the latest FW version, which introduces a risk that untested features or components may not perform as expected.
    > **Reason for Downgrade:
    > **

    - To provide more time for comprehensive testing and validation of the application on the latest FW version in a controlled environment before deploying it to QA or production.

chunks.x:

chunks.t: How to Change the Framework version for apps?
chunks.h: Step 1: Navigate to theApp Management page
chunks.x:
To update the FW version, please follow the steps outlined below.

- SelectWorkspace Hub from menu group and underWorkspace Hub, selectApp Management menu.

- Search for the app in the search bar and click on the app to get the details.

- Upon selection of App, Apps detail page will be displayed .

- Click on the edit button to make the changes /editable format.

- When selecting the App details, go to the FW version section and choose the desired version from the dropdown list.

> Note: Framework versions listed in the **popup** will be the latest three FW versions present in the current landscape.

- Select desiredFramework version and click on save. Please read the FW version release note before choosing the same.

- On clicking save button, the App FW version will be updated with the respective version selected.

> **Note**: App should be published upon changing FW version change.

Whenever there's a change in the major or minor versions of the FW platform, the apps that use the FW platform version need to be updated manually by the Application/Implementation team.

**For Example:**

We have an app named **eam_6.0.1** that uses **FW version 7_2_30**. A major enhancement is required for this app due to the recent update to the FW version.Therefore, we will create a branch for this app and all the adoptions will be done in this branch, using the latest **FW version 7_3_1**.

By reviewing the release notes for the FW update, the application team will learn about any adoptions or new features in the FW.

Once the enhancement is complete, the branch app will be merged with the latest version into a single major app version, resulting in a final product, such as **eam_6.0.3,FW version 7_3_1**. Once all necessary fixes and updates are made to the app, it will be moved to the QA branch/environment for testing.

If testing is successful, the updated app will be deployed to the production environment.

Note: How to do the app branching and merging is mentioned in the UG.

When the FW version is upgraded(major/minor) and is deployed,the applications that work on the FW version should be changed to the latest version.For that to achieve,create a branch and update the FW version as explained above. Once done with all the adoptions and changes, it is merged to the main branch and then the FW version is updated to transport it further to QA. Once the test is passed, the FW version will be updated in the application with the new FW version.

As shown in the above diagram, if the test fails, then the app will not be taking the FW update and it will downgrade to the most recent functioning version of FW to ensure everything functions properly.

During the patch upgrade in Framework platform, this upgrade will be automatically updated in all the applications which use the FW platform once they are released. So it's completely up to the FW team, when it comes to the patch update and there's nothing to do with the application team in the upgrading of FW version.

If an issue occurs after a FW update (such as bugs, crashes, or performance degradation), you may need to roll back(downgrade) the update to maintain the app's smooth functionality.

In this case we will downgrade the latest version of FW and work with the older released FW version that's working fine. For production environments, we need to revert the platform update on affected applications.

*A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.*

Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

chunks.t: Use WDIO and WDI5 for testing UI5 apps
chunks.x:
WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process

WDIO can work with any web application but lacks the awareness of the web framework that the application uses. WDI5, which is a WDIO plugin, bridges this gap and provides two key benefits, namely control locators and synchronization with the web framework. WDIO supports many types of locators - css, xpath, even plain javascript code but it lacks understanding of the UI5 controls. WDI5 exposes a browser.byControl() method that accepts a control locator and returns a proxy for the real control. Then the test can assert on the control state or even interact with the control. The second benefit is transparent but equally important – on every element interaction, WDI5 waits for UI5 rendering to complete and for the application to be completely stable.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5_1_120_27 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5_1_120_27. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

Within the closedmodules directory, establish a new folder titled klo_automation_1. Within this, create another folder dedicated to your automation, housing all requisite files needed to execute the automation.

**Note :- Adhering to this specific structure is crucial for the successful execution of the automation. The automation process attempts to access certain files, notably the klarion.json file located within the kloconfig folder, from your private node. Therefore, maintaining this structure ensures that the automation can correctly locate and utilize these files from their designated locations. Should you deviate from this structure, you will need to adjust the paths in conf.data.js accordingly to reflect the correct locations of your files.**

The files mentioned above are essential for running the automation. Let's examine each of these files individually.

Located within the kloAu directory, this file stands as the core component of the automation suite. It houses all necessary functions tasked with transforming array-formatted code into a conventional format. Since WDIO cannot interpret array formats directly, this conversion is imperative for compatibility.

This file will house all fundamental configurations necessary for the automation to operate, including user credentials, URLs, and the specific Chrome directory in which the execution should occur.

1.  baseUrl: Users must specify the URL to be accessed at the beginning of the automation process.

2.  userId: The User ID associated with the login or registration conducted on the previously mentioned URL.

3.  Password: The user's password, if applicable.

4.  desktopLoginID: For the desktop login ID, users need to supply the User ID used for logging in on their desktop.

5.  Profile_directory: Users must indicate the Chrome profile directory where they intend to run the automation.

6.  Specs: Within the Specs object, users must list the names of the specs they wish to execute, adhering to a sequential order. It's important to note that the names provided are case-sensitive. Ensure consistency in naming across all references to avoid discrepancies.

> **NOTE :- The Spec and Data file names should be entered exactly as demonstrated in the preceding example. Additionally, the object name must remain consistent. Please remember that the names provided are case-sensitive.**

7.  ReplaceMap :-This file includes all the application variables required for test cases. Variables must be declared within double dollar signs, like \$variable_name\$

##### **How replaceMap Operates in Automation:**

> In the array format data file, replaceMap searches for all variables declared either in conf.data.js or at runtime within the data file itself. Whenever it encounters a match, it substitutes the matched variable with the corresponding value from the object's key-value pair.
>
> **Note**: By default, two variables, \$dateKey\$ and \$landscape\$, are automatically created within replaceMap at runtime. These variables can also be utilized within your data file.

- **\$dateKey\$**: This variable holds the current date and time. It's particularly useful for generating unique names for entities and screens each time the automation runs. For instance, in the example provided, the \$entityName\$ variable is set to "d_autest_\$dateKey\$". During execution, %dateKey% is replaced with the current date and time, resulting in a unique identifier like d_autest_25_06_12_11.

- **\$landscape\$**: Contains the name of the landscape for which the private node was created. This value is derived from the klarion.json file, indicating the landscape's name.

This file encompasses all the scripts generated by the test recorder. Essentially, it stores the test script or code in array format that was produced.

Observing the header section of the tsData variable, we find an object containing several key-value pairs. Let's explore these details further.

- Remark: This field allows you to summarize what the entire specs entails or outlines the actions performed by the specs. A point to remember is that this summary will also appear as the specs name in the HTML report.

- Reload and Login: These should always be set to true to ensure that the login process occurs every time the automation starts.

- Menu: Used to specify the navigation path to the desired menu. The structure follows the pattern of the menu group name, preceded by a forward slash, and then the menu name. For instance, to open the Procify Data Studio inside App Builder, the menu entry would be “App Builder/Procify Data Studio”. It's important to note that both the menu group and menu name are case-sensitive.

**Note: Test Spec/Data files generated from the Test Recorder will not include the menu key-value pair in the header object. Developers must manually add this information.**

This file encompasses all the function declarations originally listed or created in the myUtil.js file. Additionally, it provides a designated space for declaring any function that is intended to be utilized exclusively within its corresponding data file.

**NOTE :- In the spec_name.spec.js file, towards the end, there's a highlighted segment shown in the accompanying image. Within the loadData function located at the bottom of this file, you must include your spec's name as a parameter. This name should precisely match the one listed under the specs section in the conf.data.js file. To ensure consistency across your files and facilitate the automation process, it's crucial to maintain identical naming conventions. Any discrepancy in naming, including variations in capitalization, will prevent the automation from initiating.**

This file will contain all the functions that you want to use throughout your entire automation. We can create function in two formats here :-

> Standard functions will adhere to the conventional coding practices of WDIO. We cannot incorporate any code snippets formatted as arrays in this context.These functions prove beneficial when dealing with non-UI5 pages, such as the registration or login pages of our servers. These functions are utilized in scenarios where there is no requirement for using replaceMap or variable replacement from a replaceMap.json file, as the standard functions do not support the replacement of variables denoted by \$variable_name\$ for ui5 pages. As demonstrated in the following example, neither replaceMap variables nor code formatted as arrays are employed, eliminating the need for runtime replacements.
>
>
>
> To grasp how we can manage non-UI5 pages or write code in a standard format, let's delve into the following:

- The \$ command serves as a concise method to retrieve a single element from a webpage.

- addValue: This function allows adding a value to an input or textarea element identified by a specific selector.

- click: Executes a WebDriver click action on the chosen element. By default, this action involves scrolling to and clicking the targeted element unless otherwise specified.

> In the subsequent example, we demonstrate the process of selecting a password field element and verifying its presence on the screen using the isDisplayed() API. If the element is visible, we proceed to insert the user's password using addValue and subsequently click the login button.
>
>

> Array format functions in the context of writing code snippets in spec_name.data.js allow for the creation of reusable functions that can be called multiple times within the file. These functions are particularly useful for performing repetitive actions, especially when those actions need to be executed in a recursive manner. In such cases, defining a function within myUtil enables you to easily invoke it as many times as needed without duplicating code. Using new test recorder that generates actions in an array format, you would parse these actions and pass them to your function.By structuring your code in this way, you can efficiently manage complex sequences of actions, especially when dealing with arrays of elements or actions generated from automated tools like a test recorder. This approach promotes code reuse and simplifies the management of repetitive tasks within your tests.
>
>
>
> Understanding functions, we recognize that they can be invoked repeatedly, each time with varying parameters. Following this principle, we too employ a similar strategy. To explore how we pass parameters, we'll initially focus on utilizing these parameters within our array format code. Specifically, we leverage the replaceMap.json file, which stores the values of parameters passed to functions at runtime. Essentially, we're retrieving these parameter values stored in replaceMap.json through a function designed for our array format code.
>
> Our methodology involves declaring a variable and importing a utility function named getWordFromReplaceMap from the kloAuWdio file into our myUtil file. This function accepts a variable name (such as \$entity\$, which is declared in spec_name.data.js) as its parameter and returns the corresponding value from replaceMap.json at runtime.

For Node.js projects, the package.json file provides a simplified way to manage a project's metadata and dependencies.

The file ensures a project always has current information about the libraries and tools it needs to work correctly.Every npm package and Node.js project has a package.json file with metadata for a project. The file resides in the root directory of every Node.js package

.The package.json file contains descriptive and functional metadata about a project, such as a name, version, and dependencies. The file provides the npm package manager with various information to help identify the project and handle dependencies. **To install the dependencies, transfer your most recent package.json file to your automation directory. Afterward, navigate to this directory using the command prompt and execute npm install.**

The configuration file contains all necessary information to run your test suite. It’s a NodeJS module that exports a JSON. No changes should be made in that file by the developer.

WebdriverIO-plugin for wdi5.

It provides the ui5-service to WebdriverIO, running tests in the browser.In case the very first called page is non-UI5 (think SAP CP CloudFoundry login), the config option skipInjectUI5OnStart can be set to true to postpone injecting wdi5 into the browser context. Consequently you have to do it later, as soon as the UI5 page to test is available. This can be done by calling injectUI5() on the wdio-ui5-service.

So, the UI5 service will prove beneficial when encountering a stale element reference error during automation, preventing the automation from halting or performing unexpectedly.

The stale element reference error is a WebDriver error that occurs because the referenced web element is no longer attached to the DOM.Every DOM element is represented in WebDriver by a unique identifying reference, known as a web element. The web element reference is a UUID used to execute commands targeting specific elements, such as getting an element's tag name and retrieving a property off an element.

When an element is no longer attached to the DOM, i.e. it has been removed from the document or the document has changed, it is said to be stale. Staleness occurs for example when you have a web element reference and Upon navigation, all web element references to the previous document will be discarded along with the document. This will cause any subsequent interaction with the web element to fail with the stale element reference error.

To overcome this ui5 service needs to be injected again in the page again. Refer to the screenshot above for more details.

chunks.h: Variables values stored using getValue() and getText()
chunks.x: When using variable names in getText() and getValue() actions, they should not be reused. Although it operates similarly to replaceMap, where initializing the same variable with a different value results in replacement, this principle does not apply when storing values from the screen using getText() and getValue() actions. In these cases, repeating variable names is not allowed.

Occasionally, due to failed automation execution or termination mid-execution, the replaceMap.json file may become empty. Consequently, attempting to run automation afterward will fail to start. To mitigate this problem, an empty object must be explicitly declared within the replaceMap.json file.

For checkboxes within a grid, the necessary wdio code is not automatically generated. To resolve this challenge, the browser.keys() APIs should be employed as a temporary fix. Leveraging keyboard actions can also help address this issue.

chunks.h: Validation for screen created in UI
chunks.x:
If users are conducting validations on a UI-created screen following a full preview, certain codes need to be made dynamic. Otherwise, the automation will not execute correctly if triggered again or under different conditions.

As illustrated in the preceding image, there are several areas (e.g., 2-3 spots) where the code requires modification to ensure successful execution each time the automation runs. For instance, consider the scenario where the automation's flavor changes; without making the code dynamic, the automation would fail. Additionally, the page name appears in both the view ID and model ID sections of the code. If a new page is introduced with a different name, the automation will also fail unless the code is updated accordingly to reflect this change dynamically.

chunks.h: replaceMap does not work after menu opening sometimes
chunks.x:
Sometimes, as noticed, once the menu is opened during automation, the process halts in the browser and begins displaying errors in the console. The primary issue here is that the replaceMap, which is intended to substitute variables for viewID and modelID at runtime, fails to do so; instead, it retains the original values provided in the spec_name.data.js file.

To update the page's viewID and modelID with the current ones, since these identifiers change with every screen navigation, the automation executes the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console. This function retrieves the current page's viewID and modelID, which are then stored in replaceMap. If a match is found, the existing viewID and modelID in the code, formatted as an array, are replaced with the current ones.

After the menu is opened in automation, the code proceeds to the next segment. Occasionally, the screen remains partially open, still showing the loading state. At this point, even though the code execution has moved forward, the screen is not fully loaded. Consequently, when the automation runs the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console, it returns the modelID and viewID of the previously viewed page, not the current one, because the page is still in the process of rendering and is not yet fully visible. In previous automation runs, registration occasionally failed silently—resulting in an "Oops" page without any visible error. Interestingly, re-registering often resolved the issue. To address this inconsistency, we’ve introduced a new checkRegistration() function.

This function verifies whether the registration process has completed successfully. If not, it automatically re-invokes the appropriate registration function to retry the process.

**Important Implementation Notes:**

- Replace the placeholder function name shown in the image with your actual registration function name.

Previously, in the automation flows, whenever a busy indicator appeared, the scripts would automatically pause and wait for it to disappear before continuing. However, in recent runs—even in local environments also—the automations have stopped waiting for the busy indicator or busy dialog to fully disappear, causing them to proceed prematurely to the next steps.

To address this issue, we've introduced the waitForBusyIndicator function. This asynchronous method ensures that the automation process pauses until the busy dialog has completely disappeared before continuing.

**Note: Our application uses two types of busy elements: sapMBusyDialog and sapMBusyIndicator. Please inspect your screen or application via the browser console to determine which one is currently in use.**

- It repeatedly checks for the presence of the busy dialog every 2 seconds (CHECK_INTERVAL).

- If the dialog is visible, it continues to wait.

- Once the dialog is no longer detected, it waits an additional 10 seconds (WAIT_AFTER_CLOSE) to confirm it doesn't reappear.

- If the dialog remains gone, the loop exits and automation continues.

- Any errors during the check will also break the loop and log the issue.

chunks.t: kloauwdio changes(au2.load and au2.save, before and after function as async)
chunks.x: In the **old code**, the load function was relatively simple and lacked safeguards against concurrent access. It directly attempted to read the file and parse its contents without any locking mechanism, which could lead to race conditions if multiple calls were made simultaneously. Error handling was minimal—if the file was missing or the JSON was malformed, it could throw exceptions or behave unpredictably. Logging was sparse, making it difficult to trace issues during runtime. The expiry logic for cached data was hardcoded to 30 seconds, which might have been too short for some use cases. Additionally, the replaceMap was updated silently without clear fallback behavior when the file was empty or corrupted.

chunks.t: kloauwdio changes(au2.load and au2.save, before and after function as async)
chunks.x:
In contrast, the **new code** introduces a much more robust and thoughtful design. A promise lock (loadPromise) ensures that only one load operation runs at a time, preventing race conditions and improving consistency. Logging has been significantly enhanced, with detailed messages at every step—file read attempts, parsing outcomes, expiry checks, and error handling—making debugging far easier. The expiry window has been extended to 10 minutes, offering more flexibility for longer-lived data. If the file is missing or contains invalid JSON, the function now logs a clear warning and resets replaceMap gracefully, ensuring the application remains stable. The save function also includes logging for both the content being written and the success or failure of the write operation. Overall, the new code is more resilient, traceable, and better suited for production environments.

The structure of the newau2.load and au2.save code are illustrated below ➖

Previously, the before and after hooks were not asynchronous, even though they invoked au2.load and au2.save. These functions have now been updated to be asynchronous, allowing proper handling of asynchronous operations within the hooks.
