chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document )
chunks.x: The **Upload Business Requirement Document** screen is the first step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this step, users select the target application, review the available AI token quota, and upload the Business Requirement Document (BRD) or Business Blueprint (BBP) that Developer AI will analyze to generate the application.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document ) > Select Application
chunks.x:
The **Select Application** dropdown displays all applications, select application with Developer AI enabled the selected application acts as the target application where Developer AI will generate all the required components.

- All AI-generated artifacts, such as entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, and configurations, are created within the selected application.

- Ensure the correct application is selected before proceeding with document upload.

**Note :-**

**1. Developer AI not Enabled for Application**

If Developer AI is not enabled for the selected Application, It will show warning that Developer AI is not enabled for that application

**2. Developer AI server is not available**

If the Developer AI Server is not running, a dialog will be displayed with the message: “*Developer AI server is currently unavailable. Kindly contact the Administration team.*”

**3. BBP Build is triggered when other BBP build is in-progress in the same application**

If Build is triggered in the same application when other BBP Build is in-progress in the same application, then also the warning will come showing the BBP Build is already in progress

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document ) > Token Quota
chunks.x:
The **Token Quota** section displays the AI token consumption details for the selected user.

A token represents a unit of text processed by the AI model. Every analysis performed on a BRD or BBP consumes tokens.

The Token Quota panel provides the following information:

- **Tokens Used** – Total number of tokens consumed by Developer AI.

- **Total Token Allocation** – Maximum tokens allocated to the application.

- **Remaining Tokens** – Tokens still available for future AI operations.

- **Usage Percentage** – Visual progress bar showing the percentage of the allocated quota that has been consumed.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document ) > Token Units
chunks.x:
Developer AI displays large token counts using abbreviated units:

Unit

Meaning

Example

K

Thousand (1,000)

250K = 250,000 tokens

M

Million (1,000,000)

2.0M = 2,000,000 tokens

**Example**

If the Token Quota displays:

- **2.0M / 26.5M tokens**

- **7% Used**

- **24.5M Remaining**

**It means:**

- A total of **26.5 million tokens** have been allocated.

- **2.0 million tokens** have already been consumed.

- **24.5 million tokens** are still available.

- Approximately **7%** of the total token allocation has been utilized.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document ) > Generate BBP
chunks.x: The **Generate BBP** feature enables users to generate a **Business Blueprint (BBP)** by simply describing their application requirements in natural language. Instead of manually preparing a detailed BBP document, users can provide a high-level business description, and Developer AI automatically transforms it into a structured Business Blueprint.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document ) > Upload BRD / BBP Document
chunks.x:
Once the application has been selected, upload the project documentation for analysis.

Developer AI supports the following documents:

- **Business Requirement Document (BRD)**

- **Business Blueprint (BBP)**

The document can be uploaded by:

- Dragging and dropping the file into the upload area.

- Selecting the file from the local system.

Once the document is uploaded, Developer AI begins analyzing its contents to understand the business requirements and extract key information required to build the application. During this process, Developer AI identifies and generates:

- Business entities

- Functional requirements

- User roles

- Application screens

- Menu structure

- Business workflows

- Notifications

- Schedulers

- Dashboard requirements

- Homepage configuration

- Relationships between business objects

The extracted information is then used to automatically generate the initial application structure within the selected Procify application.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 1 : Upload BRD (Business Requirement Document ) > Preparing a BBP for Developer AI
chunks.x:
Developer AI expects the **Business Blueprint (BBP)** to follow a predefined structure for accurate analysis and application generation. If your existing BBP is not already in this format, it must be converted before uploading.

To prepare a Developer AI-compatible BBP:

1.  Ensure you have the existing **Business Blueprint (BBP)** for your project.

2.  Refer to the **Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt** document (Prompt).

3.  Upload both:

    - Your existing BBP.

    - The Developer AI BBP Conversion Prompt.

4.  Submit both documents to **Claude** for processing. The conversion prompt has been specifically designed and validated for **Claude**, and it is recommended **not to use other AI models** for this conversion.

5.  Claude will generate a new BBP that conforms to the standardized format required by Developer AI.

6.  Review the generated BBP to verify that the business requirements have been accurately converted.

7.  Upload the converted BBP using the **Upload Business Requirement Document** section to continue the application generation process.

Once uploaded, Developer AI will analyze the standardized BBP and generate the application's foundational components, including entities, screens, dashboards, workflows, configurations, and other required artifacts.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 2 : Analyze & Review
chunks.x:
The **Analyze & Review** tab is the second step in the Developer AI application generation workflow. In this stage, Developer AI processes the uploaded **BRD** or **BBP** and extracts all the business information required to build the application.

The purpose of this step is to validate that the uploaded document has been successfully analyzed before proceeding with application generation.

Once the document analysis is completed successfully and the extracted summary has been reviewed, click Open Dashboard to proceed to the detailed review screen.

The Open Dashboard button opens the Review Extracted Information dashboard, where users can:

- Review all extracted business components in detail.

- Verify entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, schedulers, menu access, and homepage configuration.

- Modify, add, or remove extracted items as required.

- Validate the extracted information before proceeding to the Execution Plan stage.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 2 : Analyze & Review > Review Extracted Information
chunks.x:
This section provides categorized access to all the information extracted from the uploaded BRD or BBP. Each category displays the number of items identified during the analysis, allowing users to review every component before proceeding with application generation.

The available categories include:

- **Entities** – Displays the entities extracted from the document.

- **Screens** – Lists the application screens identified during analysis.

- **Schedulers** – Displays scheduled jobs or background processes.

- **Functional Requirements** – Shows the extracted business requirements.

- **Notifications** – Lists notification and alert configurations.

- **User Roles** – Displays user roles identified for role-based access control.

- **Menu Access** – Shows the application's navigation menu structure.

- **Homepage** – Displays the extracted homepage configuration.

- **Out of Scope** – Lists requirements identified as outside the application's scope.

- **AI Visualize** – Provides AI-generated visual representations of the extracted business information.

>

- **Ask BBP –** An AI-powered assistant that answers questions related to the uploaded BBP.

Selecting a category displays its corresponding details in the main content area for review.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Step 2 : Analyze & Review > Review Extracted Information
chunks.x:
**Note: At present, manual addition, modification, or deletion of extracted components is not supported. The entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, and other components displayed on this screen are generated by Developer AI based on the uploaded BRD or BBP and are used as the foundation for application generation. Users can review the extracted information before proceeding to the next step.**

Developer AI provides an option to export the extracted entity information for offline review or integration.

chunks.h: Developer AI Wizard Screen and Its Tabs > Export Options > Export to JSON
chunks.x:
The Export to JSON button downloads the extracted entity metadata in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format.

The exported file contains structured information such as:

- Entity details

- Attributes

- Relationships

- Entity types

- Associated metadata

The JSON format can be used for documentation, integration with external systems, or further processing.

**The Export to TXT option is currently not supported.**

Although the option is visible in the interface, exporting the extracted information in TXT format is not available in the current release and will be supported in a future version.

The Re-Analyze button allows users to run the document analysis again if changes have been made to the uploaded BRD or BBP, or if the extracted results need to be refreshed.

When clicked, Developer AI:

- Reprocesses the uploaded document.

- Extracts the latest business requirements and application components.

- Updates the extracted entities, screens, functional requirements, user roles, notifications, menu access, and other information.

The Mark All Review Completed button confirms that the extracted information has been reviewed and approved.

Selecting this option indicates that:

- The extracted entities have been verified.

- Screens and functional requirements have been reviewed.

- User roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other extracted components have been validated.

- The application is ready to proceed to the next stage.

**Note: Marking the review as complete is mandatory before proceeding. If this step is not completed, an alert message will appear when you attempt to continue, prompting you to mark all reviews as completed before moving to the next stage.**

The Execution Plan button navigates to the next step in the Developer AI workflow.

After the review is completed, clicking Execution Plan opens the Execution Plan screen, where Developer AI displays the sequence of activities required to generate the application.

The Execution Plan provides an overview of:

- Components to be generated.

- Order of execution.

This serves as the final review before Developer AI begins generating the application.

The Refine BBP with AI feature is designed to allow users to improve or modify the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) using natural language instructions before proceeding with application generation.

This option can be accessed by clicking the ✨ (AI Refine) button available on the Review Extracted Information screen.

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > How it Works
chunks.x:
1.  Click the ✨ (AI Refine) button.

2.  The Refine BBP with AI dialog is displayed.

3.  What should AI change? text box, enter the required modifications or enhancements in natural language.

Examples:

- Tighten the module scope.

- Add missing approval rules.

- Correct notification triggers.

- Add a new business entity.

- Update the workflow for order approval.

4.  Click Apply AI Changes.

Developer AI is designed to analyze the provided instructions and update the extracted BBP accordingly. The refined information would then be reflected in the extracted components for further review before proceeding with application generation.

**Note: The Refine BBP with AI feature is currently not supported in the current release. Although the option is available in the interface, AI-based refinement of the extracted BBP is not yet functional and will be supported in a future release.**

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Review BBP Changes Before Build
chunks.x:
After clicking Execution Plan, the Review BBP Changes Before Build dialog is displayed. This screen provides a final summary of the extracted Business Blueprint (BBP) before the application build process begins.

The summary displays the number of:

- Existing in BBP – Components that were identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP.

- Added – New components that have been added during the review process.

- Updated – Components that have been modified before execution.

The dialog also lists all the extracted application components, such as:

- Entities

- Screens

- Functional Requirements

- Notifications

- User Roles

- Other extracted artifacts

This allows users to perform a final verification of the application metadata before proceeding with the build.

Available Options

- **Compare AI Changes** – Displays a comparison between the original extracted information and any AI-generated changes (if applicable).

- **Back to Review** – Returns to the Review Extracted Information screen to make further changes or validations.

- **Proceed to Execution Plan** – Confirms the review and navigates to the Execution Plan screen, where the application generation workflow is initiated.

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Step 3 : Execution Selection
chunks.x:
After clicking Proceed to Execution Plan, the Execution Selection screen is displayed. This screen allows users to review all extracted components and select the items that should be included in the application generation process.

A summary at the top of the screen displays the total number of extracted components, including:

- Entities

- UI Screens

- Schedulers

- Workflows

- Notifications

- User Roles

- Menu Access

- Homepage

Each category shows the number of items identified from the uploaded BRD or BBP.

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Component Selection
chunks.x:
The lower section displays the extracted components grouped by category. Each item is accompanied by a checkbox, allowing users to choose whether it should be included in the application build.

Users can:

- Review the extracted entities and screens.

- Select or deselect individual components.

- Use the Select All option to include all available components for generation.

Only the selected components will be considered during the application generation process.

After reviewing and selecting the required components, click Execute to start the application generation process.

Developer AI begins generating the selected application components within the chosen Procify application. This includes creating the selected entities, screens, workflows, notifications, user roles, menu access, homepage configuration, and other supported artifacts.

**Note: Ensure that all required components are selected before clicking Execute, as only the selected items will be included in the application generation process.**

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Step 4 :Build Application
chunks.x:
After clicking Execute, the Execution Progress screen is displayed. This screen tracks the progress of the application generation process and shows the status of each component being created.

To begin generating the application, click Build Application.

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Build Application
chunks.x:
The Build Application button initiates the application generation process based on the components selected in the Execution Plan.

During the build process, Developer AI automatically creates and configures the selected application components, including:

- Business entities

- UI screens

- Value Helps

- Sample data

- Application roles

- Notifications

- Business rules

- Menus

- Homepage configuration

- Permissions

- Other supported application artifacts

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Execution Progress
chunks.x:
As the build progresses, the Execution Progress section displays the status of each component.

Each component is marked with one of the following statuses:

- In Progress – The component is currently being generated.

- Completed – The component has been successfully created.

The progress cards provide a quick overview of the build status for each application component.

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Execution Log
chunks.x:
The Execution Log records every step performed during the application generation process.

The log includes information such as:

- Analysis completion

- Entity creation

- Screen generation

- Business rule creation

- Sample data insertion

- Role creation

- Menu generation

- Homepage configuration

- Permission assignment

- Any warnings or errors encountered during the build

The execution log helps users monitor the build process and troubleshoot issues if required.

chunks.h: Refine BBP with AI > Build Completed
chunks.x:
When all selected components have been generated successfully, the status changes to Build Completed.

A confirmation message indicates that the application has been successfully created within the selected Procify application.

Users can then click Continue to proceed to the next step in the Developer AI workflow.

**Note :-**

1.  **Build Queue Notification**

> When a BBP build is triggered for an application while another BBP build is already in progress for a different application, the new build request is not started immediately. Instead, it is automatically placed in a system-wide queue and will begin execution once the currently running build is completed.
>
>

2.  **Build Already in Progress**

> If a BBP build is triggered for an application that already has an active build in progress, Developer AI does not start a new build for the same application. Instead, it notifies the user that a build is already running and provides an option to view the current build progress.
>
> Click **Yes, Show Progress** to open the ongoing build progress screen, or click **Cancel** to close the notification
>
>

**Entities**

After the application is generated, all the business entities created by Developer AI are automatically available in the Data Studio. These entities form the core data model of the generated application and can be reviewed and further configured as needed.

The left navigation panel displays the list of all generated entities. Selecting an entity opens its complete configuration, where you can review its properties, relationships, business rules, workflows, access control, and other metadata.

**Note:** If the generated entities are not immediately visible in the Data Studio, refresh the application or browser. The entities will be displayed once the latest metadata is loaded.

**Screens**

Developer AI automatically generates the required application pages based on the uploaded BRD/BBP. These pages provide the user interface for interacting with the generated business entities and application features.

The generated pages are available in the **Page Builder** and can be reviewed, customized, or enhanced using the standard Procify page designer.

In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following pages:

- **p_homepage_001** – The application's landing page that provides users with the initial view after logging in.

- **p_dashboard_001** – Displays the application's dashboard, providing a consolidated view of key information, widgets, and business insights.

- **p_delivery_mgmt** – The Delivery Management page used to create, view, update, and manage delivery-related transactions.

**Role & Users**

The roles and users generated by **Developer AI** can be viewed from the **Roles & Users** section under the **Details** tab of the generated application in **App Management**.

This section allows you to review the user roles and user assignments created for the application.

**Homepage**

Log in using one of the users created in the **Roles & Users** section. After successful login, the application opens the **Homepage** generated by Developer AI.

The homepage displayed corresponds to the configuration defined in the **Homepage** component during the application generation process. It serves as the application's landing page and provides users with quick access to the generated modules, dashboards, and navigation menus based on their assigned role and permissions.

**Dashboard**

Developer AI automatically generates the application dashboard based on the requirements defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP.

The generated dashboard provides users with a consolidated view of key business information, metrics, and navigation components relevant to the application. It is designed to offer quick access to important data and frequently used features immediately after login.

The dashboard created by Developer AI can be accessed from the **Dashboard** menu within the generated application and can be further customized using the standard Procify dashboard designer to meet specific business requirements.

**Note:** The layout, widgets, and overall design of the generated dashboard are determined by **Developer AI** based on its analysis of the uploaded BBP or BRD. Dashboard generation is AI-driven, and users cannot control or define the dashboard layout by providing screenshots or sample designs. To influence the generated dashboard, include clear and detailed dashboard requirements within the BBP or BRD.

**Menu**

Developer AI automatically generates the application's navigation menu based on the modules, screens, and user workflows defined in the uploaded BRD or BBP.

The generated menu provides users with organized navigation to access the application's features. Menu items are created based on the business requirements and are assigned appropriate access according to the generated user roles and permissions.

In the example shown, Developer AI has generated the following menu items:

- **Home** – The default landing page that provides users with quick access to the application.

- **My Deliveries** – A module for managing and viewing delivery-related transactions.

- **Dashboard** – Provides access to the application's dashboard, displaying key business insights and summary information.

**Developer AI** is an enhancement to the **Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform** that enables users to build enterprise applications by describing their requirements in natural language. Instead of manually configuring application components, users can generate applications through a single prompt, significantly accelerating the application development process.

**Developer AI** is an AI-powered application development capability built on top of the **Procify Low-Code/No-Code Platform**. It transforms business requirements, provided in natural language, into a structured application design and automatically generates the foundational components required to build an enterprise application.

Rather than requiring users to manually analyze requirements, design data models, create user interfaces, and configure application components, Developer AI automates these activities using artificial intelligence. This significantly reduces the time and effort involved in the initial stages of application development while ensuring consistency and alignment with business requirements.

When a user provides a business requirement through a prompt, Developer AI performs the following activities:

1.  **Requirement Understanding**

    - Interprets the user's business requirement using Natural Language Processing (NLP).

    - Identifies the business objective, workflows, business entities, users, and relationships.

    - Extracts key functional and data requirements from the provided description.

2.  **Business Analysis**

    - Converts the natural language requirement into structured business insights.

    - Identifies business processes, modules, and system interactions.

    - Determines the application's functional scope and required components.

3.  **Data Model Generation**

    - Analyzes the business entities involved.

    - Identifies attributes, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships.

    - Generates a normalized data model suitable for the application.

4.  **Diagram Generation
    > ** Based on the analyzed requirements, Developer AI automatically generates design artifacts such as:

    - Entity Relationship (ER) Diagram

    - Data Relationship Diagrams

    - Business Process Flow Diagrams

    - Other architecture and visualization diagrams required for application planning

5.  These diagrams provide a clear visual representation of the application's structure before development begins.

6.  **Entity Creation**

- Creates all required business entities.

    - Defines fields, data types, validations, constraints, and relationships.

    - Configures entities according to Procify platform standards.

7.  **Screen Generation
    > ** Developer AI automatically generates the application's user interface, including:

    - Data Entry Screens

    - List/Grid Views

    - Detail Pages

    - Forms

    - Navigation structure

8.  The generated screens are mapped directly to the underlying business entities and workflows.

9.  **Dashboard Generation
    > ** Based on the application's business context, Developer AI creates dashboards containing:

    - Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    - Charts and Graphs

    - Summary Cards

    - Business Metrics

    - Data Visualizations

10. These dashboards provide users with meaningful insights into their business data from the outset.

11. **Application Foundation Creation
    > ** After generating the business model, entities, screens, and dashboards, Developer AI produces the initial application structure within the Procify platform. This foundation serves as the starting point for further customization, refinement, and deployment.

Developer AI is designed to simplify and accelerate enterprise application development by leveraging Artificial Intelligence. It minimizes manual effort in the initial stages of development and enables organizations to transform business ideas into functional applications more efficiently.

chunks.t: Key Reasons to Use Developer AI
chunks.x:
- **Accelerates Application Development**

  - Converts business requirements into application components within minutes, significantly reducing development time.

- **Reduces Manual Effort**

  - Eliminates the need for manually analyzing requirements, designing data models, and creating initial application structures.

- **Converts Natural Language into Applications**

  - Enables users to describe business requirements in plain language, allowing AI to generate the application's foundation automatically.

- **Automates Requirement Analysis**

  - Interprets business requirements and extracts key business entities, workflows, relationships, and functional requirements.

- **Generates Design Artifacts Automatically**

  - Creates Entity Relationship (ER) diagrams, business process diagrams, and other visual models without manual intervention.

- **Automatically Creates Business Entities**

  - Generates entities, attributes, relationships, validations, and data models based on the identified business requirements.

- **Builds User Interface Components**

  - Automatically creates forms, screens, list pages, navigation, and dashboards, reducing UI development effort.

- **Ensures Consistency and Standardization**

  - Produces applications following Procify platform standards and best practices, ensuring uniformity across projects.

- **Improves Productivity**

chunks.t: Key Reasons to Use Developer AI
chunks.x:
- Allows developers to focus on business logic and advanced customizations instead of repetitive setup tasks.

- **Accelerates Time-to-Market**

  - Reduces the overall application development lifecycle, enabling organizations to deliver solutions faster.

- **Minimizes Human Errors**

  - Automates repetitive design and configuration tasks, reducing the likelihood of manual mistakes.

- **Supports Rapid Prototyping**

  - Enables quick creation of application prototypes that can be reviewed, refined, and enhanced based on stakeholder feedback.

- **Enhances Collaboration**

  - Provides generated diagrams and structured application models that improve communication between business users, analysts, and developers.

- **Scales with Business Needs**

  - Supports the rapid creation of applications of varying complexity while maintaining consistency and quality.

- **Provides a Strong Application Foundation**

  - Generates the initial application structure, allowing developers to focus on enhancements, integrations, and business-specific customizations rather than starting from scratch.

chunks.x:
**Date of Issue: August 2023**

Target Audience: Senior Developers.**

chunks.t: Enhance and Upgrade Your Application — Overview
chunks.x:
Applications developed need to be changed frequently to adapt to changing requirements as well as to add new functionalities.

This document will teach you how to enhance your existing applications in these scenarios.

- One must be assigned a Cockpit app to get full access to the Workspace Hub.

- The Private Node setup should be done in the user's system.

- VS code should be available in your system.

To enhance your application, you need to go through the following steps:

1.  Create a new version of the application

2.  Assign version to users (Automatic)

3.  VS Code initialisation

4.  Rollout of new application

5.  Publish the new version

chunks.t: Create a new Version for the Application
chunks.x:
Login to the Workspace Hub - User Guide

**Step 1: Select App Management under Workspace Hub**

In the Workspace Hub, use the menu **App Management** to see the list of apps available.

We will find the list of apps available.

**Step 2: Create a new app version**

Click on the app for which you want to change the version. Go to the details section.

In the details section, when you make the screen editable, you will find the **Version** Action Button of a “Released” App. Click on that to create a new app version.

When a new version is created it will inherit all the adoptions that were made in the previous version. Also, when we add new features and make changes in the new version, those changes will reflect in the new version only, making the older version obsolete or deprecated.

This can be shown with a specimen below:

We have created an app named **tech_services_app**, and we have created a new version for this app. We have added all the basic details required.

Next, we will go to the Language section. **Languages** will be adapted from the previous version only. If we need to add or remove any language in this section that can be done here.

Similarly, the **FAQ keys** will be inherited from the previous version; we can add or remove any keys as per our need.

chunks.t: Create a new Version for the Application
chunks.x:
Furthermore, we will see that once we adapt to a new version (steps mentioned above), it will inherit all the features such as the created page, entity query, etc. from the previous version.

We can check this inheritance under **Artifacts**.

**Note:** The image above shows the Page from UI Objects that have been inherited. This is because only one page has been created in the previous version.

chunks.t: Create a new Version for the Application
chunks.h: Assign a New Version to Users
chunks.x:
Once the new version is created, we will need to assign the same to the users according to their designation. Users from previous versions are added automatically. Rest you can add in the following way.

**Step 1: Add users to the upgraded app version**

To assign a new version to the users, click on the app that has had a version upgrade and go to **Roles&Users.** Under Application Roles click on the **Users** link.

**Step 2: Add New users**

By clicking on the **Add** button under the Application User section, add new users.

We will get a list of users in a popup. Select and add the required user name and **Save**.

A new user will be added to our upgraded app.

The Initialisation process will pull all the app files and controller files assigned to the workspace of the private node server.

The Initialisation process is as follows:

**Step 1:** First create a folder of the workspace. Then go to VS Code, tap F1, and select **Procifynow: Klarion IDE Setup.**

**Step 2:** The registration page will open. Give the URL (example: https://maven89.com/Klarion/u/c/V1/EAM/fs/index.html) and user credentials and **Start Setup**.

The Initialisation process will start.

**Step 3:** Once initialisation is complete a repository note will open. We will check our app.

Now our Initialisation process is complete and our app will retrieve all the necessary files.

chunks.t: Rolling the app to Assigned Users
chunks.x: When a new app version is created, that version will not immediately be made available to all the users. It will be made available to a certain group of users so that they can test and check whether the application is working properly. Once it gets verified and approved by those users, the app will be made available to the rest of the users.

chunks.t: Rolling the app to Assigned Users
chunks.h: Process to assign users > Via User Collections
chunks.x:
To assign the app to a group of users, we will use User Collections in the Workspace Hub.

**Step 1:** Create a user group by adding the basic details.

**Step 2:** Go to users and add the number of users required for this trial.

**Step 3:** We will add the **App Groups** under this particular user group and save the entire process.

**Note:** Under the **App Groups**, individual groups related to a single app get created automatically. These groups can be seen in case we click on **Show All** as shown in the image below:

If you see the image, you will find **tech_services_app** has individual groups, one for the Manager, one for the Developer, and one tester. You can assign the required group to your user group or you can create an App group separately for your app and assign the user group respectively.

chunks.t: Rolling the app to Assigned Users
chunks.h: Process to assign users > Via App Collections
chunks.x:
In case we want to create a separate App group follow the steps below:

**Step 1:** Go to **App Collections** and click on **Create Group**.

**Step 2:** Add the **Basic Details** and move to Apps.

**Step 3:** Click on the Add button. A popup will appear. Select the app or apps needed to add to the group and press the **Add** Button.

**Step 4:** Now we must select the Installation type and the Roles for the particular apps.

- **Update Type:** It specifies how the app will be installed.

- **Regular:** It installs the registered app normally for the user and creates initial sync, table generation, etc

- **On-Demand:** It helps to assign the app to the user but the user has to install the app through the Developer Page.

- **Default:** It is the same as regular installation type which helps the user to assign the app directly with table creation.

- **Upgrade Type:** It specifies how the app will be upgraded.

- **Immediate:** It upgrades the app with an immediate notification where the user will have the option of the **OK** button and it upgrades the app.

- **Postpondable:** It upgrades the app with an optional notification where the user will have the option of the **OK** and **Cancel** buttons and it will install the app later on.

- **Role:** specifies via which role the application will be assigned to the users of that group.

Once these are selected, we will move to User Groups and add our user group. The App Group is created and the User Group has also been added to the App group.

chunks.h: When do we Publish the new version?
chunks.x: When a new version of the app is created, it only inherits data from the previous versions. The other changes or new features need to be added by the users. Once that is done the app needs to be published. Doing so, the change will reflect on the relevant devices.

chunks.h: How do we Publish a new version?
chunks.x:
Publishing an app is the final step after all the changes and upgrades have been made in the new app version. Once all the page creation, entity creation, user, and role assignments are in place we can move ahead and publish the app.

For this:

Go to App Management, then select the app with its new version and click on the **Publish** button.

This is a screen in the KloTouch application that helps the users search for the queries that they face while using the application with detailed answers. This is used to edit and create question-answers and groups in an optimised way which will benefit the ultimate consumers while using the application.

This can be used to:

- Search for user-relevant questions and get answers in detail.

chunks.h: FAQs Editor — Procedure To Use FAQs Editor
chunks.x:
1. Go to the **FAQs Editor** menu and click on the sub-menu named FAQs Editor to open it.

A screen will initially load with the FAQ Groups based on their sequence in ascending order.

>

**Note:** Now the button is visible at the screen title toolbar.

On click of the Procify logo, the screen title toolbar will collapse resulting in the buttons not being visible.

2. Users can search for the FAQs based on their Group Title, Question, Key ID and Key Description. Users need to enter the relevant texts and click on the OK button to perform the search.

**Group Title:** This denotes the title under which one will find their relevant queries. Eg: If a user has a query related to **Work Order**, they can search for it under that very group.

**Questions:** This denotes any search by directly writing the question on the search bar.

**Key ID:** Key ID helps us get the element which we want. Each Flavor will be associated with one or more keys and based upon those keys, groups will be loaded for that flavor. Each key can be used in multiple flavors.

**Key Description:** It is a relevant and memorable description that we put for the key ID.

>

3. Users can clear the search criteria by clicking on the cross button in the search bar.

4. Users can expand any group to see the list of questions associated with that group by clicking on the dropdown.

chunks.h: FAQs Editor — Procedure To Use FAQs Editor
chunks.x:
5. Users can click on the add button beside the search bar to create a new group. After clicking on the button, a popup will appear and the user needs to select a key to which this group will be associated.

**Note:** These Keys are created and maintained in the *Account Console*. In case you do not find the key you are looking for, kindly go to the Account Console and create the relevant key.

6. Users then need to select a key and then click on the Create button. Users will be navigated to the detail section where they have to fill in the group title (mandatory), sequence, and icon and then click on the **Save** button.

7. Users can also edit the group details by clicking on the Edit button on the right side of that particular Group Title.

>

8. Users can then update the group details and then click on the **Save** button again.

9. Users can delete a group by clicking on the delete button on the right side of that particular group title. Upon clicking it will ask the user for confirmation.

On giving the delete confirmation it will delete the group along with its entire associated question.

10. Users can create a new question inside a group by clicking on the add button at the right side of that particular group title.

chunks.h: FAQs Editor — Procedure To Use FAQs Editor
chunks.x:
11. Users then need to fill in the device type (mandatory), sequence, Question Title (mandatory) and answer and then click on the **Save** button. By default, the language will be set to English.

12. Users can edit a question by clicking on that particular question link.

Users then need to make the changes and click on the **Save** button.

13. Users can also delete a question by clicking on the delete button on the right side of that particular Question Title. It will ask the user for the confirmation.

Upon user confirmation, it will delete the question.

>

14. Users can also create the language variants of a particular question by clicking on that particular question title and then clicking on the language button in the Question Detail section.

On clicking on the language button the user will get a language selection popup where they have to select the language in which they want their translation.

15. After the selection of language a popup will appear where on the left-hand side the English variant of the question will be visible and on the right-hand side, the selected language variant will be visible.

**Note:** If the question in the selected language variant is already created then it will open in edit mode otherwise it will open in create mode.

After filling in all the details, the user can click on the save language button to save all the changes.

Users can click on the close button in the top right-hand side of the popup to close the language popup.

**Scheduled Tasks**, **Jobs**, and **Job Execution Log** together form the core components of a **Job Scheduler**, which automates, monitors, and logs job executions, ensuring that tasks are completed on time and according to predefined rules.

- A Job definition is a screen where the job’s templates are created, set/scheduled and kept systematically.

- A **Job** refers to a specific execution of a job. Each time a job is run, a new instance is created. It represents the occurrence of that job with its unique execution parameters, timestamps, status, and related metadata.

- A **Job** allows you to track the job's progress, its start and end time, and its outcome (whether successful or failed). Each Job is distinct and can be tracked individually.

- A **Job Execution Log** contains detailed records or entries related to the execution of a Job. It provides a step-by-step log of events, actions, and messages generated during the execution of the job.

- **Job Execution Logs** are useful for debugging, auditing, and understanding the behavior of a job during its execution. They typically include information like warnings, errors, and system outputs that occurred while the Jobs was running.

**Note:** We follow the FreeFormatter Cron Expression Generator, which uses Quartz-style 6/7-field cron syntax.

* * * ? * *

Background jobs are classified into four categories: -

- **Class S (System):** A class system for fw jobs. System jobs are not part of the quota

- **Class A (Critical Priority)**: - Some tasks are urgent or critical and must be scheduled with class A priority jobs. Class A priority reserves one or more background work processes. Users must decide how many background work processes should be assigned to Class A priority jobs.

- **Class B(Normal Priority)**: - Once Class A jobs are completed, Class B jobs will start executing in the background before Class C jobs.

- **Class C(Low Priority)**: -It runs after class A and class B jobs are completed.

Data object in KloBase Datastore is known as entity. An entity has one or more named properties, each of which can have one or more values. Each entity in KloBase Datastore has a key that uniquely identifies it.

In simple words we can say Entity is a database table. In dbms we store data in the form of a table containing information about entity type like order, address etc. In an order database, a table containing information about all the orders. For example, orders have properties like customer, Amount, products, etc they are attributes which combined make table.

One entity must be part of one and only one BO.

Types of Entity:

- Persistent Entity: Entity which physically exists/stored in database as a table. Fields in Persistent Entity could be either Persistent or Transient.

  - Persistent Entity by default Tenant Dependent can be made Tenant Independent

  - Persistent Entity by default or User Dependent can be made User Independent

- Transient Entity: It is an in memory entity that doesn’t exist in a database. All fields in Transient Entity are Transient only. It can be constructed out of query result or by code to hold the value at runtime. Messages can’t be communicated through Middleware using Transient entity.

- Config

- FW only Types

  - Archive

  - History

Provide a unique entity name and mark if it is a Root entity. Root entity is considered as a BO. To define an entity you need at least one entity property, It could be either transient or regular(persisted in DB).

Entity attributes:

- **Entity Name :** Unique ID across all flavors.

- **Is Root :** This defines the Root entity of a BO. BO Name is the same as Entity Name if this is marked TRUE.

- **Entity Type:** Persistent/Transient.

- **Network mode** : This is optional here and inherited from flavor this entity belongs to. You can overwrite if required.

- **BO Name :** Root entity name. Entities in the same BO should have a primary relation.

- **Is metadata** : This decides whether it is a meta model entity or transactional. If marked TRUE, framework creates table in metadata DB. Otherwise in transactional DB.

- **Has appvariant :** Starts following the flavor behaviour. If is_metadata FALSE, by default has_appvariant is FALSE and not allowed to change.

- **Has Tenant** : Entity starts following the Tenant behaviour. if TRUE, s_tenant_id field will be added in DB table at the time of the update schema.

- **Is Config** : if TRUE, this is considered as config entity.

- **Has Config** : Framework will provide a config entity which can further customized with configuration fields. If object type is not applicable this is an object type independent config. Config is accessible in application by using *entityInstance.config *

- **Has created fields :** To know what time facts are recorded to database and by whom. if TRUE, s_created_on and s_created_by fields will be added by FW at the time of update schema. These two fields are filled by a system of entity creation.

> UI: s_created_on is server time in UTC format when record created and s_created_by is the logged in user.
>
> Message processing: Created On gets updated with server time(UTC format) if blank otherwise accept from message and Created By will be taken from message.
>
> Background Job/Upload: Created On gets updated with server time( UTC format) when record got created. Created By is the user by which Background job scheduled.
>
> Archive Data: accept created on/By field’s values from transaction entity as is.

- **Has modified fields :** This is to record the last changed time and user. if TRUE, Modified On and Modified By fields will be added by FW at the time of update schema. System updates these fields on every create/change of entity.

> Change in a BO:

- In case if any change on root/header level only, this updates only header table modified fields.

- In case any change is made to the child entity, this updates the parent entity also upto root.

> UI: same as created fields.
>
> Message processing:
>
> Background Job: same as created fields.
>
> Archive Data: accept all values from transaction entity. If an object is modified during the archiving process, then modify fields get changed accordingly.

- **Check Dirty:** re-evaluate all entities for dirty before calling on update. Default value: ?

- **Has Brand :** Entity is brand dependent or independent. if TRUE, s_brand field will get added by FW at the time of update schema.

- **Has Object Type :** Entity follows Object Type behaviour. if TRUE, s_object_type field of type int(11) gets added by FW at the time of update schema.

- **Has Status :** if TRUE, s_status and s_status_custom fields will get added by kloBase at the time of update schema. See more details in the Status section.

- **Can create/read/update/Delete:** if TRUE, insert/read/update/delete is allowed in the table otherwise not allowed. Applied only on Server side. Server side Exit and MW still allows even if false.

- **Can read all** : if TRUE, read all values allowed from the table otherwise not allowed. Applied only Server side. Exit and MW still allows even if false. Runtime query will not work if it is FALSE.

- **Has History:** This is to maintain the changing history of an BO. If TRUE, it creates a separate blob or transactional table to maintain the history of all changes. Every change on an entity gets captured in the history table and the main transactional table holds only the latest record. Table name starts with ‘h’.

> Only on root entity or full BO?
>
> Maintain change history only for specific status?
>
> Object type based configuration?
>
> Is this supported offline?

- **Has Archive:** This is to facilitate the data archiving. This can be enabled only on the root entity/ BO. Always complete BO gets archived.

> Table name starts with ‘a’. One more table created as a view which starts with ‘v’ to fetch transaction and archive table data as union.
>
> If the ID series is exhausted?

- Server Side: Push data from transaction table to Archive table. Which means data will get deleted from the main table once moved to the archive table.

  - Maintain configuration based on which data to be archived.

  - Background job scheduler to push data from transactional table to Archive table. While archiving no dirty objects are allowed.

  - APIs: *archive().* This API will work only on server side.

  - clearArchive() : this deletes all records from the archive table.

  - Update to offline endpoints. This deletes the entity in local DB.

  - ON_ARCHIVE event.

  - Query: by default query fetch data from transactional table(d table) but if archiving is enabled, users can explicitly mark to fetch archived data. This is a union of both transactional and archived tables.

  - IsArchived flag is returned TRUE by framework if data is from the archive table. This flag can be used by application to highlight archived data or disable edit option.

- Do not allow the archived records to be updated. Framework throws an error if any dirty object found for archived records.

  - Value help/ Association relation for archived masters. Example:

  - Update transaction entity: this should adjust the archive and view.

    - Add/Delete new property

    - New relation/ Delete relation

- Client Side: delete data in client DB(local) and do not send any updates to the server.

  - API: *deleteLocal()*

- *kloQuery has deleteLocal();*

> Dependency: Does not allow you to archive until the related(supplied by application. Do not follow entity relation) object gets archived. Dependency is decided based on aggregate relations. Helper function to be written by Application to check if any dependent object exists.

- **Has Time Dependent :** At any given point in time, an entity has a value for each of its attributes. If the values of any attribute for an entity may change over time and you are interested to know the value of an attribute at a particular point in time, it is meaningful for entities to have properties exactly when they exist and mark the entity as time dependent. In case if you are interested only in the current value of the attribute, do not mark as time dependent.

> This is to maintain the periodic(time dependent) data with valid time. If any entity is marked as time dependent, framework creates below three fields in the table. In a BO any entity can be time dependent.

- s_valid_from(Timestamp) - Validity start date and time. Part of the primary key. Default is the current date.

- s_valid_to(Timestamp) - Validity end date and time. Default value is 31-12-9999.

- s_active(boolean) - the latest record will be marked as TRUE.

> At a time only one entry should be active and the validity period should not overlap for two records. By default Valid from is current date but can be changed.
>
> Past date: Config to be maintained for past date is allowed or not. Message processing(from SAP, device or to device) follows the config for the past date. If allowed it accepts the date from message or UI otherwise it changes the FROM date to current.
>
> If first entry, except the values provided from UI or Message and mark active flag TRUE.
>
> In case of update, modify the current existing active record’s s_valid_to accordingly(based on s_valid_from the new record). Also mark current entry active flag FALSE and new entry as TRUE. Both update and create should be in the same transaction.
>
> Mainly this will be used for master data tables where periodic data is required. For example, pricing, user address, etc. MRP/Pricing of a product can be changed periodically.
>
> Can not be changed based on object type or flavor. This can be defined only in owning flavor of an account.

- **Approval :** In case if approval is required for a BO, at the time of creation of the BO it should not change the current record. Once it is approved, then only it gets activated. To consider this scenario, a separate blob table is maintained for ‘To Be Approved’ objects. Once final approval is done it will get moved to the main transaction table and activate. If enabled, approval flag will be provided from the framework.

  - This is applicable for time dependent and time independent both entities.

  - Configurable on object type based.

> Workflow will be discussed separately later.

Entity Property describes the attribute/member variable in an Entity(field in the database table) and holds the value in runtime. It has a Property ID(name) and Property type. The Property Type defines the data type and behaviour of the property.

Entity Property’s attributes define the behaviour of the property. Entity properties can be added or archived only in the owning flavor of an account. Below are the parameters:

- Entity Property ID: unique within an entity across all flavors. Can’t be changed later.

- Property Type/Element ID: select the existing Property type or create new. This defines data type, field length, precision, etc. It can be changed only in the owning flavor of an Entity. Selection of a domain, size and property type:

  - Choose existing

  - Extend from

  - Copy and override: copy any existing property type and change the parameters. This makes a copy of all attributes except Property Type ID.

  - Create New

- Type: Regular / Primary Key / Transient Field / Calculated Field /System Fields. / Secondory Key

- Value Help: select already defined Value help ID. Wherever this property ID is binded in UI, VH is automatically applied. Can be overwritten in the screen field.

- Is restricted Value: Restrict the input value within the associated VH. Tri value: None, Strict(UI and BOL), Suggestions(Only UI side). (Note: Moved this to Entity property from Property type).

- Is Mandatory: Empty or Null values are not permitted during entity creation/update. Does not force in UI as mandatory. Non Key mandatory fields are not necessary for select.

- Default Value: Default value will be populated immediately after creating new Entity. \$ Variables can also be used.

- ID Series: mention the ID series here if applicable for this field.

Naming convention:

- Max length allowed for property ID is 31 char.

- Only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) are supported.

Entity property ID starting with ‘s_’ is reserved for systems fields by framework.

- Persisted : Property which physically exists/stored in the database as a table column. Persisted Property owning Entity also has to be Persistent Entity only.

- Transient: transient property is a runtime attribute only. Use this to hold some value at runtime. Example: query result alias value, value filled or determined in rule, from UI set and get attribute.

- Primary key: primary key of a table. Values of set of primary key fields must be unique. If field is primary key, isNull/Nulable property will be marked as false automatically.

- System Defined Properties: based on the relevant flags in entity definition, framework provides standard columns in a table. Field name, Data Type, Label, etc are already defined and no changes allowed here. Developers can’t add a system field.

Property Type is to define the behaviour of Entity Property(Database Table field) and Screen field. It is a reusable unit. Property Type has below attributes:

- ID : Unique ID of Property Type within Landscape.

- Domain: select Domain ID from predefined list to define the data type.

- Length and precision of the field. Precision is applicable only for decimal data type. Specify length for decimal and ‘chr’ types.

**Reuse**: To define the common behaviour of multiple Entity/Query Properties, Property type can be reused across entities.

It should be reused if entity properties are logically the same.

- Ordered Qty and Del Qty - not to use the same property type. But Ordered qty in two diff tables should share the property type.

- Property type should be different for Vendor and Customer fields in the same or diff entity. Both should be extended from BP ID because data type should be same for all.

- It is recommended to use the same property type for a field which is used in multiple tables as foreign key. To understand this better let’s take an example of the Material Code field which is part of Material master as a primary field but also part of other tables like Order and Logistics items.

**Authorization:**

Authorization is to restrict the access of data, for logged in user. Authorization on any entity of a BO is applied on the whole BO. Authorization is defined on Property Type and applied for all queries the Entities wherever that Property Type is used.

Do not apply Authorization on Query Property.

For example, logged in users should be able to see only the Orders that belong to them. Below is the Entity definition:

| Entity  | Entity Property | Property Type |

| d_order | order_id        | order_id      |
| d_order | order_date      | order_date    |
| d_order | customer_id     | cust_id       |
| d_order | net_amount      | amount        |

Here apply the authorization on “cust_id” Property Type to filter the orders of particular customers. If the same Property Type is used at other places, authorization will be applied on those entities also.

In case you do not want to apply the authorization at all entities or apply the authorization at only one place, then extend the base property type and create a new Property Type.

In case if authorization is applied on more than one property or multiple value in one property. Below is the behaviour:

1.  AND Operator: If authorization is applied on multiple properties in the same BO with different property types, all parameters will be ANDed.

    1.  Example1: There are two properties in d_order entity customer and sales_person both have different property types. If authorization is applied on both, this will be ANDed.

2.  OR Operator: Used a property type with multiple entity properties in the same entity, all parameters will be ORed. (Reuse property type within entity). At the same time it will be ANDed with other parameters.

    1.  Example2: There are two properties in d_order entity customer and vendor both have the same property type, in this case both parameters will be ORed.

3.  IN Operator: If Multi values qualified for one property, all values will be considered with IN operator.

1.  Example3: Authorization is set on state field in d_order entity and multiple values passed at runtime, in this case all values will be passed with IN operator.

Entity relation is to allow one entity to relate with another entity qualified by entity property. Relation has a unique name within the Entity.

- Association: An association is a structural relationship which connects one entity with another. Given an association between two entities, can navigate from one entity to the other entity and vice versa. Association relations can be across BOs. By default each relation is of type Association if it is not marked as Aggregated or Primary.

> Example1:

- d_order_item(source)

- d_material_master(Related)

> Create a relation to show the material description, LOB, or other property of material.
>
> Example2:

- d_order_item(source)

- d_order(Related)

> If you want to navigate from order Item to order header. Define a relation between Item as Source and Header as Related entity.

- Aggregated Relation: Aggregation is a type of association where two entities(tables) are tightly bound. In some cases we might come across “whole-part” relationships between two Entities, in which one entity is a part of another entity. Such a relationship is known as an aggregation. An aggregation relationship can be described in simple words as "an object of one class can own or access the objects of another class." If a parent is deleted/archive, all other parts associated with it are deleted. Aggregate relations can be across BOs.

- Primary Relation: This is a special kind of aggregate relation within BO boundary. All entities in a BO are navigable from root entity once unidirectional and only once. Below are the use cases of primary relation:

  - Message processing

  - Key mapping

  - Find Parent

A Rule is a function that is to be executed after another function has finished executing. Rules are written by Developer as per the application business logic. Rules can be subscribed with either Entity or Query.

**Define the Rule:**

- Define a rule with below inputs

  - Rule ID - unique ID across all entities.

  - Class - file name

  - Mime Type: Java or JS

  - Description

- Recommended to Define the rules on the root entity of BO.

- Each Rule returns a promise. Promise should be resolved or rejected based on the application scenario.

> Example: resolve the promise if updated successfully and reject in case of any error.

>

**Subscribe Rule:**

You can subscribe to the Rule for any Entity which can be executed based on the Event type assigned. Rule subscription is part of kloIDE. To subscribe a Rule you need to provide below details.

- Exit(Rule) ID: Select existing rule on BO, General, All or create a new rule.

- Exit Class: file name. Defaulted from rule definition for existing rule.

- Mime Type: Java or JS. Defaulted from rule definition for existing rule.

- BO Event Subscription ID: auto generated?

- Event Type:

  - Entity

    - ON_CREATE

    - CREATE_NEW_FROM_TEMPLATE : execute only if executeCreateFromTemplate() method called from application.

    - ON_UPDATE : execute only on update entity.

    - ON_DELETE : execute only on delete entity.

    - BEFORE_MAPPING

    - AFTER_MAPPING

  - Some additional Event types on Root Entity(BO)

    - ON_SUCCESS : execute only after the successful transaction of a BO.

    - ON_ERROR : execute only if the transaction failed for a BO.

    - ENDPOINT_RESOLVER : this is to get all the endpoints to push the MW message. This gets called on every create/update/delete of a BO.

- Object Group: Thi is optional and If Object Group is not specified, it will get called for all objects of that entity.

- Channel Type: there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule.

  - All

  - Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server

  - Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON CLIENT

  - Endpoint/Device to Klarion Server---ALWAYS ON SERVER

  - Endpoint/Device to Server/Client---NETWORK CONTEXT SWITCH

  - Klarion Server to Klarion Offline Server

  - Klarion Server to Klarion Server

  - Legacy to Klarion Server

- Sequence No: Decides in what sequence Rule to be executed. In case multiple Rules subscribed, sequence of rule execution is followed. All positive numbers(1-n) excepted.

  - If sequence no. is the same for 2 rules : should not allow from IDE.

Same rule can be subscribed multiple times with different Channel types.

**Execution sequence of rule:**

If any change in DataSet of an Entity at any level of BO. All Entities which are on top as per BO definition(sequence of entities) are set to WriteSet till Root entity which we call dirty object.

- Rule will be executed for all dirty objects one by one. Each record in an entity invokes the Rule.

- Execution is from Leaf Entity(of BO) Rule to Root Entity Rule for all WriteSet.

  - First call all rules of Lowest level( Leaf Entity in a BO) Entity.

  - If multiple BO changes are there in one WriteSet, first execute the rules of lowest level entity in all BOs then next up… then next up

- At the same level rule execution is as per sequence number( 1 is top priority).

- Execute rule based on Channel Type

- Again jump to Child entity Rule if any modification in parent entity Rule.

Same rule subscribed multiple times?

Control Transaction in rule:

- Cancel Transaction Refresh Changeset : This cancels the full transaction and refreshes the Changeset/Writeset.

- Stop Exit chain only for current entity Instance

- Stop Exit chain only for current BO instance

- Eliminate the object from writeset (refresh entity/BO using refresh(deepRefresh)) : if new entity?

- Eliminate the BO from writeset (refresh BO)

- Flush Changeset (commit) : intermediate commit

kloQuery is a meta model for fetching the data from the data store, like SQL in RDBMS. For example, the entity ( table) name “d_order” has multiple columns including “s_status”. To fetch all the record for open order in RDBMS need SQL as “Select ord_id, qty, ord_date from d_order WHERE d_order.status = ‘open’ Orderby ord_date ASC” and execute to get the desired result.

kloQuery behaves similarly with a few value added services, it gives the ability to fetch the data seamlessly for offline applications and online applications. Abstracts out multiple syntax of Odata, SQl, Json etc. so that programmers can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short hand optimization like pagination column select. Security features like authorization etc..

Runtime Query does not need modeling. It inherits behavior from entity and BO definition and operates with API. Later we will consider more control on query by modeling the kloQuery.

kloQuery is made with Query, QueryProperty, PropertyType, Select, orderby etc.. It returns kloEntityset. kloEntityset is an array of kloEntities.
For e.g. consider following SQL

| SELECT ord_id, qty AS ord_qty, ord_date FROM d_order WHERE d_order.status = ‘open’ Orderby ord_date ASC” |

| Let q = await oController.getQueryP(“d_order”);
q.setProperty(“d_order.status”, ‘open’);
q.setOrderBy([{fieldname:”d_order.ord_date” , sort_type:”ASC”}]);
Let result: kloEntitySet = await q.ExecuteP(); |

Above SQL needs to be represented by kloQuery. WHERE clause of SQL d_order.status is the input search criteria modeled as query property and property type of the query property will describe the type(string) caption and value help. Similarly kloQuery also has OrderBy and Select together with other constructs to hold the SQL constraints. Query objects are directly bindable in UI for user input and capable of providing label and value help. kloQuery can be represented by premodeled query by name and at runtime enhancing with constraints.

Authorization is the process of giving someone permission to do or have something. In multi-user systems, authorization defines for the system which users are allowed access to the system and what privileges of use.

Authorization can be defined on Property Type only. Authorization can’t be defined on object type or some other parameter. In case if you want to add/remove/change authorization on base property type, extend the property type in separate flavor.

Define the authorization at Entity Property Type to apply on all the queries of a BO where that particular Property Type is used in Entity Property definition. Property type can be used in multiple Entities, in this case authorization will be applied on all queries of these Entities.

For example, ‘user_id’ is a property type and this is used in ‘user’ column definition of multiple Entities(tables) like d_order, d_logistics, etc. Now all the queries where the return entity is ‘d_order’ or ‘d_logistics’, you will get the filtered result based on user logged in.

Authorization is applied on the whole BO irrespective of return Entity. If authorization is defined on any child/root entity it will be applied on all the entities which are part of that BO.

When used as string literal in meta model in authorization it is replaced with real value. E.g. \${\$USER.login_id} will be replaced with currently logged in user id. Similarly authorization can be applied on other \$VARAIBLES also. For more details refer \$VARIABLE section.

\$Variable is available in Rule and Endpoint resolver but not available while processing middleware messages.

Syntax: \${\$.\}

**Rule Execution:** Authorization is applied when query runs inside BO Rule on server side. In case of client side Rule execution authorization is not applied as client DB should have only filtered data. If any client(endpoint) is not authorized to see the data it should not get synced to the client. Which means authorization is applied at the time of **initial sync and data(message) push to client**.

**Inherit Authorization:** Authorization of parent object added automatically to the child. This means if authorization is applied based on customer_id property type on order Entity, the same will be applied on the child entities(upto n level) also.

Authorization is applied in Read and Create operations. As it is applied on Read operation, Delete operation is covered under this. User can’t delete the data which is not allowed to read.

Authorization is not applied while querying data in middleware message processing as the system does not know the User.

Authorization is not applied to scheduled jobs as the user configured in Job is common.

APIs to be provided to get the \$variable values in non-odata call.

Authorization has to be applied on Upload data.

How to skip authorization in one particular scenario? Can be useful in debugging in development system.

Data archiving is the process of moving data that is no longer actively used to a separate storage device for long-term retention. Archive data consists of older data that remains important to the organization or must be retained for future reference or regulatory compliance reasons.

Every attempt to create, update, or delete an entity takes place in the context of a transaction. A single transaction can include any number of such operations. To maintain the consistency of the data, the transaction ensures that all of the operations it contains are applied to KloBase Datastore as a unit or, if any of the operations fails, that none of them are applied. Furthermore, all strongly-consistent reads (ancestor queries or gets) performed within the same transaction observe a consistent snapshot of the data.

In today's modern world omni channel application supporting multiple form factors and tolerance to network is a must. To support the diversity of device/hardware, OS, Servers, Clouds etc.. we end up creating one application multiple times. For any business application underlying data is a back bone. Unlike old 3 tier application architecture KloudBase promotes micro service with stateless models. This architecture gives tremendous portability and infinite scalability to meet modern needs. With in built klobroker it also enables distributed computing hence multiple system owners can easily exchange their data among themselves to form the network.

kloBO refers to mid tier in kloudBase architecture. It is based on the meta model. It accelerates the application development by providing configurability, override, run anywhere ( browser, android app, iphone app, windows mobile app). Developers can write the business rules in JavaScript and based on the deployment model kloBO runs it. kloBO is stateless hence provides infinite scalability and redundancy. kloBO also provides the authorization for security.

kloBO consists of a few core objects like Entity, Query, Rule, Transaction, Value Help and configuration etc.

Query as name refers are similar to database query. It is used for fetching data from a database. To understand it better let’s go with example I have an entity ( table) called “d_order”. It has multiple columns including a column named “state”. I want to fetch all the record where state == “open”

In db term I will write sql as “Select * from d_order WHERE state = ‘open’” and execute to get the desired result.

Query also does the same with a few value added services like it gives the ability to fetch the data for offline applications similar to online application. Abstracts the multiple syntax of Odata, SQl, Json etc. so the programmer can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short hand optimization like pagination column select. Security features like authorization etc..

For general purpose understanding, we can see it like below. Following mapping only helps to kick start with assumptions.

- Db Table: Entity definition

- Db Table’s Column: Entity Property definition

- Data type of column: property type with domain

- Business logic: Rule

- Commit: Transaction.save

- Rollback: Transaction.refresh

- Db SQL query: kloQuery

- Execute Query: kloQuery.executeP()

- Result of SQL execution: EntitySet behaves as array of entity

- Row of sql result: entity

- Value of column in a result row: entity’s property

ID Series are customizable in application during configuration hence it supports override or selection of id series based on Brand and Object Type. Application can maintain multiple entries of ID Series ( Entity, Property, [Object Type], [Brand] -> ID Series). Most accurate matching ID Series definition is picked by kloBase for further processing based on precedence first to object type next to brand.
For example, the “Order” Object has maintained the following.

- ID series “order_base_series” with no Brand and no Object type

- ID series “order_b1_series” with “B1” Brand and no Object type

- ID series “order_ot1_series” with no Brand and no “1” Object type

- ID series “order_b1_ot1_series” with “B1” Brand and “1” Object type

Object type abbreviation? \$objecttype.abr

If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 1 then order_b1_ot1_series definition will be picked for processing .
If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 2 then order_b1_series definition will be picked for processing .
If the order instance in question belongs to B2 and object type 3 then order_base_series definition will be picked for processing .

- Highest: Exact match of ObjectType and brand

- Medium: Exact match of Object type and Brand as “All”.

- Low: Object type “All” and Brand as “All”.

- Lowest: no key allocated.

An attachment is any file or document that you upload against any object. Attachment component is used for uploading and downloading the mime(images, videos, audio, pdf etc). This is an entity level flag and it indicates that attachment is allowed to store against the entity. If enabled, the attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. Users can only add/Edit/delete attachments when the component is in edit mode.

1.  Framework adds primary relation with attachment link entity and the Entity where attachment is enabled. Relation name is ‘attachments’. Within one BO, Attachment Entity can have relations with multiple Entities like order_hdr and order_items both are attachment enabled.

2.  Uploads a file in a common folder(local) and also maintains a link with the object.

3.  Mime gets pushed to the server repository via middleware.

4.  If the parent object is deleted, it deletes the attachment also but not the mime. Mime might have reference with another attachment.

5.  Attachment with new entity: as attachment is part of the same BO, commit and rollback works like other entities in a BO. Mime upload to the local folder is separate and it does not rollback if the transaction is canceled or failed.

6.  To upload or display the attachment UI controls are part of kloTouch.

This method allows to attach a new message processor, A message processor is a class which intakes a downloaded message and builds the BO structure out of it and persist these BO/Entity.

When middleware starts processing the downloaded message from server, based on the download process count, messages are read and the message processor callback is invoked with the messages, Now then the MessageProcessor class is responsible to deal with the message and resolve when the message is processed or reject in case of error so that middleware can continue processing the next message and handle error on the current message.

kloudBase supports a rich set of network modes. Two most frequent network modes are online and offline.
**OnLine** network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) communicating with server for every need. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. If Screen needs to show open Orders, kloBO will go to the server to get the data for Open Order and give it to UI for display. Similarly all the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving.
**Offline** network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. Application stores the relevant data locally and keeps the local cache and server data updated as and when finds the connectivity. Browser and installed mobile app both are offline capable.

**Cached Online** network mode refers to the capability of client communicating with server for every need but speedup the interaction by suggesting data from local cache.

**Commit Online** network mode refers to the capability of client serving the data from local cache but save always goes thru online and also modifies local cache.

**SAP Online** refers to the capability of all the transaction goes to SAP via gateway server.

**SAP Cached Online**

End users log in to the application using the client. On desktop users may use a web browser to open an online application. Hence the browser is client here. Users may install the android app on mobile and login to use offline application, hance android app is client here. Each client is identified by a unique id called **endpoint ID**.

On server physical data may need to be hard partitioned across a set of people. Normally in a multi organization scenario each establishment owns a tenant. Each tenant has a unique end point id assigned.One tenant can also host the data for multiple organizations.

End point enables the klobroker to send and receive the message across various participants. Endpoints are identified by end point ID. When a user logins into an application, installed app, needs to communicate with the server hence each installation (apk) gets a unique endpoint ID. Similarly each browser also gets endpoint id.
