Business Object (BO) is a logical unit used in a business. It is made up of one or multiple entities. E.g. If we take an invoice (bill of purchase) it consists of header and purchased items. Header and item entities ( tables) are required to store this information. Either item or header alone does not make any sense. So invoice header and invoice item entity together makes the invoice BO.

BO is a hierarchical tree of entities. Each entity must belong to one and only one BO definition. BO has only one root entity (top level). Rest of the entity (child entity) are aggregated into root or other entities to construct the entity tree.

Root entity represents the BO, root entity name becomes the BO name. Root entity also takes the full responsibility as BO apart from it’s entity responsibility.There are BO rules which are executed on root entities only like EndPointResolver, Success/ Fail / message mapper etc.

kloBroker always transmits the full BO in the Message. When any entity becomes dirty it pulls parents till root within BO in writeset. Deletion of any entity instance deletes all the cascaded agrragaed entities instances.

Primary relations are used between entities to bundle to construct entities tree in BO. All participating instances are traversable by primary relation with in BO. and each object can be visited only once. Primary relation represents aggregation with 0..n cardinality. BO tree is made of entity as node and primary relation as connector.

In authorization all the authorization upon parents up to root are also applied except the middleware message process.

Example:

- d_order (root entity/BO)

  - d_order_item (child entity)

    - d_order_conditions (child entity)

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API.

**This document provides guidance on how to correct this issue and ensure that your code follows the correct API usage patterns.**

Dialogs opened via the **KloController.openDialog** API should be closed using the **KloController.closeDialog** API, not the **sap.m.Dialog**'s **close** method. The **sap.m.Dialog's close** method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the **sap.m.Dialog.open()** method.

chunks.t: Action Items for the Application Team
chunks.h: KloController closeDialog — Action Items for the Application Team > Identify the dialogs opened using KloController.openDialog:
chunks.x:
- Review the code to identify all instances where dialogs are opened using the **KloController.openDialog** API.

- Ensure that dialogs opened using **KloController.openDialog** are only closed using **KloController.closeDialog**.

- If you find any occurrences of **sap.m.Dialog.close()** being used on dialogs that were opened using **KloController.openDialog,** replace these calls with **KloController.closeDialog**.

- If the dialog was opened using **sap.m.Dialog.open()**, it is correct to call the **close()** method directly on the **sap.m.Dialog** instance.

chunks.t: Action Items for the Application Team
chunks.h: KloController closeDialog — Action Items for the Application Team > Ensure consistency:
chunks.x:
- After making the changes, test your application to ensure dialogs open and close as expected without causing any inconsistencies.

- If there are any other custom dialog handling mechanisms or libraries involved, ensure that their behavior aligns with the standard usage of **KloController.openDialog and KloController.closeDialog.**

- After correcting the code, please perform the following tests to ensure the dialog functions as expected:

  1.  Open a dialog using **KloController.openDialog**.

  2.  Close the dialog using **KloController.closeDialog**.

  3.  Ensure that no errors or unexpected behaviors occur.

By following the above instructions, you will ensure that dialogs opened using the **KloController.openDialog** API are closed consistently and correctly with the **KloController.closeDialog** API. This approach helps avoid potential issues and improves the stability and maintainability of the application.

The KloMultiCombo box control is commonly used to enable users to select one or more options from a predefined list. The control provides an editable input field to filter the list, and a dropdown arrow to open the list of available options. The select options in the list have checkboxes that permit multi-selection.

- The user needs to select one or more options from a long list of options (maximum of approximately 200).

- The values of the option list contain secondary information that does not need to be displayed right away.

chunks.h: Usage > Do not use the kloMultiCombo box if
chunks.x:
- The user needs to choose between two options, such as ON or OFF and YES or NO. In this case, consider using a switch control instead.

- You need to display more than one attribute. In this case, consider using the kloInput instead.

- The user needs to search on multiple attributes. In this case, consider using the kloInput instead.

- Your use case requires all available options to be displayed right away, without any user interaction. In this case, consider using checkboxes instead.

- You want to enable users to add custom values. In this case, consider using the multi-input field.

- Your use case requires more options to choose from. In this case, consider using the multi-input field, either with the select dialog or value help dialog (for more than 1000 items).

The kloMultiCombo box is optimized for keyboard and mouse interaction.

The input field (2) can display a placeholder text (6) when it’s empty, or a token (1) if a value is selected.

***Components of the kloMultiCombo box***

The dropdown button (3) collapses and expands the dropdown list.

The option list (7) contains a list of selectable options (5). Clicking the label of an entry closes the option list and creates a token for the selected option. To enable multi-selection, every entry also has a checkbox (4). Clicking a checkbox creates a token. The option list remains open.

chunks.h: Behavior and Interaction > Select a Value
chunks.x:
There are three ways to select an item from the list:

- Tick the checkbox (option list remains open).

- Click the label of a select option (option list is closed).

- Use the keyboard (spacebar or Enter).

The user clicks the input field to place the cursor in the field (1). Clicking the down arrow displays the list (2). As the user types into the input field, the list is filtered accordingly (3). The arrow up and arrow down keys move the focus within the list (4), while the typed text remains in the input field. Selected options are automatically entered into the input field as tokens (5).

If the user selects items from the filtered option list (3) by clicking the checkbox or by pressing the space bar on the keyboard, the text entered in the input field remains. The option list stays open. If the user selects items by clicking the label or by pressing Enter, the entered text is cleared and the option list is closed.

The shift key can be used to select a range of items (shift+click marks the end of the range, shift+arrow up / shift+arrow down extends or narrows the selection range in the corresponding direction. Ctrl+A selects or deselects all items. If selecting all items is a common use case, you can also show a Select All checkbox at the top of the list (property: showSelectAll).

If tokens have been selected, and the multi-combo box is not in focus, the input field displays as many tokens as possible in the available space. If more tokens have been selected, an [n] More label indicates the number of hidden tokens. The tokens in the input field appear in the order in which they were selected.

Clicking the [n] More label opens a popover below the input field, in which all selected items are shown. The user can deselect an item by clicking its checkbox or label.

If the length of the last selected token exceeds the width of the input field, a label [n] Item/s is shown when the field is not in focus.

Clicking the [n] Item/s label opens a popover below the input field, in which all selected items are shown. The user can deselect an item by clicking its checkbox or label.

If there is only one token in the input field and its length exceeds the width of the input field, the text is truncated. Clicking the token opens a popover below the input field, in which the full text of the token is shown.

chunks.h: Behavior and Interaction > Filtering the Option List
chunks.x:
When the user starts typing in the input field, the option list is filtered. Only items that match the characters entered are shown in the dropdown list. The default filtering method is “starts with per term”, which matches the beginning of each word in an item’s text.

If the filtered option list contains items that start with the characters entered by the user, the first matching, unselected item is auto-completed in the input field.

Don’t use the placeholder attribute as an alternative to a label. This is important because the placeholder text will be overwritten as soon as the form is filled out. Labels are necessary because they indicate the meaning of the form fields if the placeholders are no longer visible. Show a placeholder only if the user needs a hint about what data to enter. Don’t repeat the content of the label. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format. For more information about how to use the placeholder, see input field.

Keep the label of an entry in the select option list as short as possible because the list uses single lines only. Values that are too long may be truncated. If you need to indicate that none of the selection options are selected, show a blank input field. Define a default selection whenever possible. The kloMultiCombo box cannot display columns. If you want to show two values in the option list, show the leading information first, followed by the secondary information in parentheses, such as Walldorf (Germany).

Don’t disable items in the option list. If an item can’t be selected, hide it.

You can adjust the width of the option list to some extent. The multi-combo box control is usually used in forms, where the width is determined by the form element or container in which it is embedded. Therefore, we don’t recommend defining a fixed width, but rather working with proper layout containers such as the form, simple form, or responsive grid layout, and with the layout data property, where the width is defined. If you need to restrict the width to a defined value, set the width accordingly. Keep in mind that there’s no horizontal scrolling in the option list. Entries that are too long are truncated and users won’t be able to read them. To avoid this, you can enable wrapping (property: wrapping).

additionalTextList, textList and keyList:

**keyList** accepts the value which is the property in the value help suggestionItems. When provided property goes as relative binding to the suggestionItems aggregation. And the value is the key for the suggestion items.

**textList** accepts the value which is the property in the value help suggestionItems. When provided property goes as relative binding to the suggestionItems aggregation. And the value is the text for the suggestion items.

**additionalTextList** accepts the value which is the property in the value help suggestionItems. When provided property goes as relative binding to the suggestionItems aggregation. And the value is the additional for the suggestion items. showSecondaryValues property needs to be set to true so that the additionalText is shown in the suggestionItems.

**Class**: KloInput

Extended from **sap.m.Input**,

KloInput combines the behaviour of **KloInputF4 (used for selecting an item from a list of suggested items in a valuehelp dialog)**, and **KloInputAutoComplete (used for autocomplete of a text from the suggestion items)**, **KloComboBox (used for selecting an item from a dropdown list)**, **sap.m.Input**. To Behave as KloInputF4 KloInputAutoComplete or KloComboBox the entity property must have a **value help** otherwise no value help will be displayed for the control.

We need to set the **vhType** either in the **Page Data Model** section or in the properties panel with the options **(F4**, **AutoComplete**, **ComboBox** or **None)** specified on the KloInput control so that it can behave as per the users’ requirements.

However, the vhType specified in the properties panel **overrides** the vh_type in the PageDataModel section.

**dependantProperty** is used the same way as KloInputF4 and KloInputAutoComplete.

When a dependent property is provided, it clears the set's value for that dependent field. If any field is dependent, it clears the field for that input control.

**keyList**, **textList** and **additionalTextList** properties determine if the key, description or additional description is to be displayed as value in the input control.

For vhType **Combobox**, hitting down arrow button on the keyboard within the focused input control, opens the dropdown with the suggestionItems

|

| **vhDownloadformat**        | Array of Object | -                | The vhDownloadFormat property lets developers configure how individual Value Help (VH) fields are exported during the standard Excel download by specifying key, description, or key + description for each VH field (for example: [{"my_key":"key"},{"country_code":"desc"},{"state_code":"key-desc"}]). Only the VH fields listed in this property follow the configured format, while all other VH fields use the default download behavior. |

**Fig:** Add the Excel Config via the context menu for the grid/cardlist section

You can provide the fileName in which you want the xlsx file to be downloaded.

You can maintain the xlsx file in the path **kloTouch/resources/ExcelTemplates** and provide the **templateFileName** in the **KloSectionXlsx** config to **download the template file.**

**Note:** You need to provide the required Excel templates to the infra team, they will place it in the path **kloTouch/resources/ExcelTemplates**.

If no excel template is provided in the above mentioned path, an excel template based on the visible columns in the screen will be created and downloaded.

If the excel template should contain all the columns, then please set the property “**allColumnsUpload”** in the excel config as true.

Events for KloSectionXlsx can be accessed from the events tab after adding excel config in Procify Page Builder. Currently there are two events available to the application developers:

This event will be triggered when the excel data has been converted to raw JSON data. The application developer can access this raw data and perform modifications based on their needs. The modified data (or lack thereof) will then be sent to the server for further validation and creation/modification of entities.

| **NAME**    | **TYPE** | **DESCRIPTION**                                                             |

| **rawData** | Object   | Raw excel data in JSON Format                                               |
| **errors**  | Object   | Errors (if any) can be passed that will then be displayed in the error log. |

**NOTE: This is a synchronous event. It does not support asynchronous await calls inside the function. If await is used, the event will continue with its execution without waiting for the results of the async function. If data is modified after the await call, modified data will not be sent to the server for processing. If errors are attached after the await call, attached errors will not reflect in the error log.**

**Incorrect Usage Example:**

In the above example, due to the await call to an asynchronous function, the data will be sent to the server for processing before modifying the data.

This event will be triggered after the processing of the excel file is done and the OK button of the excel upload dialog box is clicked.

IMPORTANT: Transnode Binding Requirements

> For Excel download functionality to work correctly, the following binding requirements MUST be followed:

The section with Excel download must be bound to an EntitySet transnode

> All controls within the section MUST be bound to properties of the same EntitySet transnode

Controls MUST NOT be bound to properties of a different transnode using dsrc (data source) binding

Correct Implementation Example

| **✓ Correct Binding**                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | **✗ Incorrect Binding**                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| **Section:** Bound to 'CampaignContacts' (EntitySet)**Column 1:** ContactName → CampaignContacts.ContactName**Column 2:** Email → CampaignContacts.Email**Column 3:** Status → CampaignContacts.Status**Result:** Excel download works correctly | **Section:** Bound to 'CampaignContacts' (EntitySet)**Column 1:** ContactName → CampaignContacts.ContactName**Column 2:** Email → ContactDetails.Email (dsrc binding)**Column 3:** Status → CampaignContacts.Status**Result: Excel download FAILS** |

The Menu Editor table includes a search field above the menu tree to help locate a specific Menu ID or Menu Text quickly.

**How search works:**

- The search matches against both **Menu ID** and **Menu Text**, and applies partial/fuzzy matching — you don't need to type the exact full value.

- If your search term matches a **parent** menu item only, the filtered tree shows just that parent row (its children are not pulled into the result unless they also match).

- If your search term matches a **child** menu item, the filtered tree shows that child along with its parent, so you always retain context of where the item sits in the hierarchy.

**Note on the child-count indicator:** The number shown next to a parent menu item always reflects the **total number of children that parent actually has** in the full menu tree — not just the ones currently visible in your search results. This count does not change based on your search filter. For example, searching for a parent's name may show a count of 3 even though none of those 3 children match your search text and are therefore not shown below it.

**Tip:** To view all children of a parent, clear the search field (or expand the node directly) rather than relying on the search result or the count next to it.

An **Upsert** operation refers to the combination of **update** and **insert** actions, where data is either updated if it exists or inserted if it doesn't.

When syncing messages, an **Upsert** scenario behavior typically involves checking if a message already exists in the destination system or database. If it exists, the system will update it; if it doesn't, the system will insert it as a new record.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Message Monitor > 1.5.Upsert > 1.5.1.Upsert Behavior in Middleware for Syncing Messages:
chunks.x:
* **Data Creation and Update:**

  * If the data is new (does not exist in the system), a new entry will be created.

  * If the data already exists, the existing record will be updated instead of creating a new one.

* **Upsert for Root Business Objects (BOs) and Primary Relations:**

  * Upsert is only applicable for Root Business Objects (BOs) and their primary relations.

  * For non-primary relations, the Upsert operation will work only if the relation is established using primary keys.

* **Parent-Child Relationship:**

  * If a parent is new, but the child data related to the parent already exists, this is considered an unexpected scenario. The user must handle this manually, as it is not automatically managed by the middleware.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Message Monitor > 1.5.Upsert > 1.5.2.Delete Scenario Behavior:
chunks.x:
1. **Parent Entity Deletion:**

   * If the **parent entity** is deleted, the **child entities** will only be deleted if the user explicitly sends the **isdeleted** flag as **true** in the request body for both the parent and child entities.

   * This applies to both **primary** and **aggregate** relationships.

2. **Child Entity Deletion:**

   * If the **child entity** is deleted, only the **child** will be deleted. The parent entity will remain intact.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Message Monitor > 3.0. Troubleshooting failed messages
chunks.x:
Messages that are failed to process can be found in the error q. The error can be found in the error message. Possible reasons a message can fail are.

1. Application logic - When an application logically rejects a request for processing the message. I.e. Adding items to a closed order. Adding shipments to a closed Delivery etc.
   **Suggested solution :** Find the root cause why these messages are generated. Eg. screen still allows adding items even if the status of order is closed. And fix the issue / add validation in the client side also.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Message Monitor > 3.0. Troubleshooting failed messages
chunks.x:
2. Application bugs - Some cases where application code has a bug, due to which an exception can be raised the message will fail. Eg. Improper null handling, wrong API parameters, typo etc.
3. Transaction User not configured - File processing, transaction user has to be configured with required application & permissions. As all the messages are processed based on the access of the user, messages generated by files need a user to validate against. Refer to the Landscape Editor for how to configure the transaction user.
4. Configured user doesn’t have application assigned : When messages from SAP / File processing are failing with **“Access denied: user lacks permission to the required application.”** error, it means, the user (SAP communication user / File processing user) does not have that flavor assigned to them.
5. Database Deadlock / Lock Timeout Errors:
   -    When the middleware encounters a transient database deadlock or lock wait timeout (e.g., "Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction"), messages are automatically retried up to 3 times with a 1-second delay (default values) between attempts.
   -    If all retries are exhausted, the message will move to the error queue.
   -    It will have an error message like - "Message \ failed after 3 retry attempts due to Lock wait timeout exceeded" or "Message \ failed after 3 retry attempts due to Deadlock found".
   -    The retry settings are configurable via config.json:
       "MiddlewareRetrySettings": {
           "DeadlockRetryCount": 3,
           "RetryDelaySeconds": 1
       }

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.1. Multiple Logins Can Create Active Endpoints
chunks.x:
When an application team logs in from multiple or random devices without properly deboarding the previous devices, those devices can continue to be considered active endpoints.

As a result, messages may continue to be generated for these endpoints even though the application team is no longer actively using them.

Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Whenever any new user registers in the application, a new endpoint ID is created against that account... when they log in again the status becomes Active." Each login is a distinct endpoint; none are deregistered automatically on crash or app closure.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.2 Messages Can Accumulate in the Queue
chunks.x:
Because these endpoints remain active, messages generated for them may not be synchronized with the device immediately. Over time, a large number of messages can accumulate in the queue.

This can give the impression that a large number of messages are stuck.

**Platform Reference:** Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — In-Queue is defined as "all the data that are currently present in the device_q and which are not processed yet." A high In-Queue count reflects endpoints awaiting sync, not failed or lost messages.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.3. Messages Are Synchronized When the Device Becomes online
chunks.x:
When the corresponding device comes online , the queued messages are synchronized with the device.

Once the server successfully sends the messages and receives the required acknowledgment from the client, the messages move to Success.

If the device is offline, the messages remain in the queue until the device becomes available.

Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — device_q entries move to device_log_q (Success) or device_error_q (Failed) only after processing; until then they remain In-Queue, consistent with holding messages for an offline device until it reconnects.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.4 Device-Side Processing vs. Server Status
chunks.x:
A message can reach the device successfully, but the actual processing on the device may still fail.

From the server's perspective, the message can be marked as Success when the client acknowledges that the message was received while the device was online. Therefore, Success on the server does not necessarily mean that the message was successfully processed by the application on the device.

Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — "In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success." This confirms Success tracks the send/acknowledgment, not on-device application processing.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.5 Application Team Awareness
chunks.x:
The application team may not be aware that previously used devices are still registered as active endpoints. This can result in messages continuing to be generated and queued for those endpoints.

Note: This is a training/visibility gap rather than a platform defect. Recommend making Sections 1–4 of this topic available to application teams so "stuck message" reports can be self-diagnosed before being escalated as incidents.

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.6 Automatic Endpoint Cleanup Scheduler
chunks.x:
A scheduler runs every Sunday to clean up old endpoints.

Note: The scheduler currently deboards endpoints that have been inactive for more than 7 days.

Once an endpoint is deboarded, its corresponding entry is removed from the endpoint table.

| Property | Value |

| Class name | deboardInactiveUsers |
| CRON expression | 0 0 0 ? * SUN *  (every Sunday at midnight) |
| Current inactivity threshold (this environment) | 7 days |
| Platform default threshold | 15 days — this environment has been configured below the default |
| Channel type | BOTH, unless restricted to DEVICE or BROWSER |
| Table cleaned up | Endpoint's entries removed from madm_ep_apps |

Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Deboard Inactive Users": CRON Job Expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN *, class deboardInactiveUsers, parameters No_of_inactive_days {default: 15} and Channel_type {default: BOTH}; "this scheduler will deboard all the users who are inactive since given days and it will delete the entry of all deboarded endpoints from madm_ep_apps."

chunks.h: Message Monitoring — Device Message Flow > 2.7 Scheduler Customization
chunks.x:
If the default 7-day cleanup period does not meet the application's requirements, the scheduler can be customized to use a different endpoint deboarding period.

To change it:

1. Go to the job-instances page in Cockpit and locate the deboardInactiveUsers job.

2. Open the job instance's parameters.

3. Update No_of_inactive_days to the desired threshold.

4. Update Channel_type if the cleanup should be restricted to a specific channel.

5. Save. The new threshold takes effect on the job's next scheduled run (the following Sunday, per the fixed CRON expression).

Note: The CRON schedule itself (currently fixed to Sunday) is a separate setting from the inactivity threshold — changing how often the job runs, as opposed to how many inactive days it waits, would need to be confirmed as in-scope for this customization request.

Notification is an alert message like SMS, email and notification in an app. Notification can be sent whenever it is required. This will work similarly to an endpoint resolver (it can send notifications to multiple receivers). The notifications sharing service is done by a third-party service (fcm) provider to clients. However, the data storage, the notification body, and the channel types are all configured by us.

The types of notifications we deal with are as follows:

- Email notification

- SMS notification

- Application Notifications or Push Notification (fcm)

**To Send a notification,** the Notification template should be created first, Refer to this Notification Modeler document to know more about modeling the notification template.

**Note on In-App/Push Notification Delivery:** In-app and push notifications are delivered only to users who have an active login session (i.e., a registered/active endpoint) at the time the notification is triggered. If a user is not logged in when a notification is generated, they will **not** receive it retroactively upon a later login — the notification is not queued or replayed for that user. This is intentional platform behavior, approved by both Framework and Application teams. Developers should account for this when designing workflows where a notification's relevance persists beyond a single session (e.g., by using entity-based flags/screens instead of relying solely on the notification queue for critical information the user must eventually see).

addNotification is a transaction/eventContext API which can be used to trigger notifications to the users. This can be used to trigger SMS, EMAIL and push notifications for a given set of users with a specific template. addNotification should only be called on the server environment. This API will trigger a notification, it will add a notification to the queue, and it will be picked and processed based on the queue. So, use addNotification for triggering notifications which are not immediately required. Eg. the Status update, Report generated notification,...

Do not use for:

Triggering time critical notification which has to be sent immediately. Notification triggered with this API will be added to the queue and will be processed later based on queue/service availability. To trigger the notification immediately, use sendInstantNotification.

**Note:** After calling addNotification(), you need to call commitP() with the same transaction to ensure the notification is committed and the email is triggered.

addNotification(template, entObject?, userObject?, to_list?, cc_list?)

> Notification template ID should be provided for the template. A notification template can be created using Notification Modeler.
>
> To know more about how the user object & the template are being mapped refer to this section.

> An object is an entity object from which data can be used to replace the template variables.

> UserObject can be used to provide custom properties to the template which are not provided by the object. The same properties from entObject will be overridden by the userObject.

> to_list is an array of strings (user_id / mobile number/email id) to which the notification has to be sent. If none is provided the current env user will be taken. Email, mobile, and Endpoints of the user will be used from the user details with user_id. If email is disabled or the template is not present, all email IDs in the list will be ignored. If SMS is disabled or the template is not present, all mobile numbers in the list will be ignored. mobile number/email address / Push notification endpoint is pulled from the user ID. If the App is enabled, all the endpoints will get the push notification.

> cc_list is only used for email.
>
> Example:

public async onCreateInvitation(event: EventContext){

this.txn.addNotification('invitation_template', null,{user_name:this.first_name+" "+this.last_name},[this.user_id])

}

sendInstantNotification is an EventContext API which can be used to send notifications immediately. This can be used to send SMS, EMAIL and push notifications for a given set of users with a template. **sendInstantNotification** should only be called on the server environment(server-side callBack). This API will send a notification immediately. So, use sendInstantNotification for triggering notifications which are immediately required. Eg. OTP, Task Assignment,...

**Do not use:**

For triggering regular (non-urgent) notifications. For adding the notification to the queue to be sent, use addNotification

For tracking regular changes or logging. This is an expensive functionality.

**API:**

> Notification template ID should be provided for the template. A notification template can be created using {elink Notification Modeler documentation}.

> An object is an entity object from which data can be used to replace the template variables.

> UserObject can be used to provide custom properties to the template which are not provided by the object. The same properties from entObject will be overridden by the userObject.

1.5.Scheduled Notification: > How to create a scheduled notification;
chunks.x:
To schedule a notification using the **addNotification** API, follow these steps:

1.  **Create the Notification Template:**

- The notification template is created through the **Notification Modeler** and usually contains details such as the title, body text, and any dynamic content like variables **(e.g., {{user_name}}, {{event_name}})**.

2.  **Use the templateId to schedule the notification:**

- Once the template is created, it gets a unique identifier **(templateId)**. You will use this **templateId** when calling the API to schedule the notification.

3.  **Make an API Call** to schedule the notification:

- **Call the addNotification API:** This API allows you to schedule a notification for a future time. You’ll need to specify parameters such as the message content, **cc_list, to_list.**

4.  **For recurring message notifications,**

- We first create a job in the **job definition screen** (job scheduler) and define the **cron expression** to specify the required time for sending the notification.

- Next, we create a **.ts** file inside the scheduler folder, where we implement the **onExecute()** method as outlined in the attached document.(Job scheduler) Within the **onExecute()** method, we call the **addNotification API** to send the notification.

chunks.h: 1.5.Scheduled Notification: > How to create a scheduled notification;
chunks.x:
- The **cron expression** determines the schedule for triggering the job at the specified intervals. Once the job is added to the scheduler, it will execute automatically at the defined times.

- In the scheduler, onExecute method, call **addNotificationAPI** with the template ID, objects, and the list of users / emails ID to whom the notification should be sent.

Notification callbacks let you attach files to outgoing emails. They are split into two layers: the Entity Callback (which triggers the notification) and the Notification Callback (which adds attachments). Follow the three steps below to set them up.

chunks.h: Step 1: Register Callbacks in Notification Center
chunks.x:
Open the Notification Center, select your template, and go to the Callbacks tab. Add a row for each callback method you want to call, and set the sequence number to control the order in which attachments are added to the email.

1.  Open Notification Center and select (or create) your notification template.

2.  Go to the Callbacks tab.

3.  Click Add and enter the callback method name (e.g. attachInvoice). This name must exactly match the method you write in the notification callback file.

4.  Set the sequence number. Callbacks run in ascending sequence order — seq 1 runs first, seq 2 runs second, and so on.

5.  Click More Info on the Callbacks tab to see the list of allowed attachment file types before uploading.

6.  Save the template.

chunks.h: 1.7. Multi-User Push Notification Handling (Switch User) > Switch User Behavior on click of Notification Tray:
chunks.x:
When a notification tray is clicked, the app checks whether the currently logged-in user matches the notification's target user:

- **If the users match** → the notification opens normally.

- **If the users don't match** → a **"Switch User"** warning dialog is displayed, showing:

  - The notification's intended user

  - A prompt to switch to that account

  - A warning if there are any unsaved changes (dirty objects) that will be lost on switching

  - If the user transaction has no dirty object:
    >

  - If the user transaction has any dirty object(s):
    >

- **If the intended user is in the background** (i.e. present at that device), then after clicking the “Switch User” button, it will redirect the user to the **login page**.

- **If the intended user is NOT in the background** (i.e. device clear-cache scenario), then after clicking the “Switch User” button, it will redirect the user to the **registration page**.

chunks.h: 1.7. Multi-User Push Notification Handling (Switch User) > Viewing Missed Notifications After Login:
chunks.x:
When the intended user logs back into the device, they can review all notifications that were received while they were inactive. These missed notifications are available in the **Notification Centre**, accessible via the **bell icon (🔔) at the top of the screen**. This ensures no notifications are lost, even if they were received when a different user was active on the device.

**NOTE:** After clearing the application data, the entries will be removed from the Notification Centre.

Training Version Number: 7.0
Target Audience: Developers, Clients.**

The Callbacks tab is available within a notification template in the Notification Editor. It allows you to register server-side callback methods that run when the notification is being processed, enabling you to attach files dynamically to outgoing emails. Each callback method is defined by a name and a sequence number that controls the order in which it is executed.

*Callbacks tab inside a notification template in Notification Editor*

**What you can do in the Callbacks Tab**

- View all registered callback methods for the template, listed in the execution sequence.

- Add a new callback by entering a method name. This name must match the method implemented in the notification callback file.

- Delete an existing callback by selecting it and clicking Delete.

- Reorder callbacks by dragging and dropping rows in edit mode. The sequence number determines the order in which methods run and the order attachments are added to the email.

- Click the More Info button to see the list of allowed attachment file types. Only files with allowed extensions will be attached to the email — others are silently skipped.

**Key Rules**

- The method name entered here must exactly match the method name written in the notification callback file, which extends KloNotification.

- Sequence numbers control both execution order and attachment order in the final email.

- Reordering is only possible in edit mode. Drag handles appear on each row when edit mode is active.

- Callbacks with disallowed file types are skipped gracefully without failing the notification.

For implementation details, code examples, and how to write the callback file, refer to the ***Notification Developer Guide**.*

**ODATA SERVICES**

*User Guide*

This document provides a comprehensive reference for OData services in the Procify platform. It clearly outlines which operations are supported, which are not supported, and provides practical examples for the application development team.

This user guide is designed to help application developers understand and correctly implement OData service calls It includes authentication mechanisms, supported query operations, error handling, and best practices.

| **Service URL Pattern** | https://{customer}.procifynow.com/odata/{landscape}/{fvid}/{entityname} |

| **Authentication**      | Bearer Token (OAuth 2.0)                                                |
| **Content-Type**        | application/json                                                        |
| **OData Version**       | OData v4.0                                                              |

The following OData operations are fully supported and tested in the Procify platform:

| **Operation**     | **HTTP Method** | **Description**                       |

| **CREATE**        | POST            | Create new entity with JSON body      |
| **READ (All)**    | GET             | Retrieve all entities from collection |
| **READ (By Key)** | GET             | Retrieve single entity by primary key |
| **UPDATE**        | PATCH           | Partial update of entity properties   |

| **Query Option** | **Description & Usage**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| **\$filter**     | Filter results using logical operators
Example: GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$filter=Age gt 30
Example with multiple conditions:
GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$filter=Age gt 25 and Status eq 'Active' |
| **\$select**     | Select specific fields to return
Example: ?\$select=FirstName,LastName
GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$select=FirstName,LastName,Email,Department                                                                                           |
| **\$orderby**    | Sort results by field(s)
Example: ?\$orderby=LastName asc
GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$orderby=Department asc,LastName asc
GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?\$orderby=created_on desc                      |
| **\$top**        | Limit number of results returned
Example: ?\$top=10
GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$top=5&\$orderby=created_on desc                                                                                                                         |
| **\$count**      | Include total count in response
Example: ?\$count=true
GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$count=true&\$filter=Status eq 'Active'                                                                                                               |

| **Operator** | **Meaning** | **Example** |

| **eq** | Equal to | Age eq 30
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age eq 30
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?$filter=OrderTotal eq 1500.00 |
| **ne** | Not equal to | Status ne 'Inactive'
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Status ne 'Inactive' |
| **gt** | Greater than | Age gt 30
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age gt 30
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?$filter=OrderDate gt 2026-01-01
 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?$filter=OrderDate gt 2026-02-17T01:00:00.000Z

For date supports both edm.Date and edm.DateTimeOffset format. |
| **ge** | Greater than or equal | Age ge 30
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age ge 30 |
| **lt** | Less than | Age lt 40
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age lt 40 |
| **le** | Less than or equal | Age le 40
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age le 40 |
| **and** | Logical AND | Age gt 25 and Status eq 'Active'
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age gt 25 and Status eq 'Active' |
| **or** | Logical OR | Status eq 'Active' or Status eq 'Pending'
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Status eq 'Active' or Status eq 'Pending' |
| **not** | Logical NOT | not (Status eq 'Inactive')
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=not (Status eq 'Inactive') |
| **contains** | String contains | contains(Email, 'example')
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=contains(Email, 'procify') |
| **startswith** | String starts with | startswith(LastName, 'Sm')
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=startswith(LastName, 'Sm') |
| **endswith** | String ends with | endswith(Email, '.com')
GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=endswith(Email, '.com') |

The following OData features are **NOT currently supported** in the Procify platform. Please avoid using these in your applications:

| **Operation**          | **Reason / Alternative**                                                                                                                             |

| **DELETE**             | **NOT SUPPORTED.** Procify does not support entity deletion via OData. Use alternative deactivation/soft delete mechanisms provided by the platform. |
| **PUT (Full Replace)** | Not supported. Use PATCH for partial updates instead.                                                                                                |

| **Feature**             | **Reason / Alternative**                                                    |

| **\$batch**             | Batch operations not supported. Submit individual requests.                 |
| **\$apply**             | Data aggregation is not supported. Perform aggregations on the client side. |
| **\$search**            | Full-text search is not supported. Use \$filter with contains() function.   |
| **Actions & Functions** | Custom actions and functions not supported. Use standard CRUD operations.   |
| **\$skiptoken**         | Server-driven pagination not supported. Use \$filter                        |
| **\$format**            | Only JSON format supported. XML, ATOM formats not available.                |
| **\$expand**            | Use flat entity and filters                                                 |

These features have limited support with specific constraints:

| **Feature**             | **Limitations**                                                         |

| **Date/Time Functions** | Only year(), month(), day() functions supported. No hour/minute/second. |

Important Points:

1.  Primary Key Handling:

    1.  If the Primary Key value is provided in the request payload, the existing record will be updated.

    2.  If the Primary Key value is not provided or not matched, a new child record will be created under the respective parent entity.

2.  Relationship Cardinality Support:

    1.  For **1::1 relationships**, the related entity must be provided as an object. **Array or null values are not supported** for 1::1 navigation properties.

    2.  For **1::N relationships**, the related entity must be provided as an array having the object(s)

3.  PUT Method Behavior:

chunks.h: UPDATE Operation Example > Request Body (With Relational Data)
chunks.x:
1.  When using the **PUT** method, missing non-mandatory, non-primary properties will be populated with their **configured default values**.

    2.  **If no default value is configured**, the property will be set to null.

    3.  **Previous Behavior:** it was directly setting the value to null for the missing non-mandatory, non-primary properties.

4.  Transaction Handling:

    1.  Parent and child entity operations are executed within a single transaction. If any validation or processing error occurs, **all changes are rolled back**.

5.  Invalid relation IDs or property names in the request body are silently ignored with a warning logged, allowing the valid parts of the update to proceed.

6.  \$expand in URL:

    1.  GET with \$expand returns parent along with nested child entities in response.

    2.  URL Exmaple: [https://fwtest.procifynow.com/odata/UT/odata_test_1-0-2/d_e1('01332d8cc3913b2f8848462c095e1e37')?\$expand=d_e1_d_child_aggregate_1_1,d_e1_d_child_primary_1](https://fwtest.procifynow.com/odata/UT/odata_test_1-0-2/d_e1('01332d8cc3913b2f8848462c095e1e37)

However, the deep update operation will still complete successfully, since \$expand only controls the response representation and does not affect the update operation itself.

chunks.x: For **Grid**, **Tree**, and **Auto Grid** section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. chunks.t: Automatic Alignment Handling for Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid Sections
chunks.x:
If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is **Integer** or **Decimal**, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value **Right**.

This automatic alignment is applied only when:

- The control is an input-based control.

- The control is bound to a property of domain type **Integer** or **Decimal**.

chunks.t: Automatic Alignment Handling for Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid Sections
chunks.x:
During updates, if:

- A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or

- A new binding is added to the control,

the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly.

1.  **Entity**: Entity defines a single entity (single row in a database table).

2.  **Entity Set**: An entity set is a set of entities (an entire table in a database).

3.  **Query**: Query which is associated with the entity.

4.  **Other**: Other types of transnode represent that the node is not associated with any entity. Its data can be bound from the controller.

1.  **Blank**: If the model path is marked as blank then the data will not be set to its folded path.

2.  **First**: If the model path is marked as first then the first index of its entityset(folded from) will be set.

3.  **History**: If the model path is marked as history then it records the active index of the entityset.

> For example: if the model path is marked as history, then each selection of entity will be recorded.

4.  **None**: If the model path is marked as none then the data will not be set for that path.

Set active is classified into three categories as listed below:

1.  **Always**: Always defines navigation without any pre-conditions except menu navigation.

2.  **Saved**: Saved means navigation is permitted only if there is no dirty object in the transaction. If dirty entities are found, the Save confirmation dialog comes to ask the user if he/she wants to save the changes, otherwise, navigation is cancelled.

3.  **Valid**: Valid is a default value. Valid means navigation is permitted if there are no dirty objects or dirty objects are in a valid state with no error. If dirty objects are there and in an error state, the errors are highlighted on the page for the user to correct before moving forward. If the mode path’s set_active_if is provided as “valid”, on time of navigation the onValidate function (if the function is maintained in the .ts file) will be called.

Please refer to the below matrix for all combinations of set_active_if:

|                      |                                                   |                | **always**                    | **saved**      | **valid**     |

| **Within Screen**    | **Same index of entityset(tab selection change)** | **CREATE**     | No Validation, No Dirty Popup | No Dirty Popup | No Validation |
|                      |                                                   | **Not CREATE** | No Validation, No Dirty Popup | Dirty Popup    | Validation    |
|                      | **Different index of entityset**                  | **Any**        | No Validation, No Dirty Popup | Dirty Popup    | Validation    |
|                      | **Close Detail**                                  | **Any**        | No Validation, No Dirty Popup | Dirty Popup    | Validation    |
| **Different Screen** | **Through Manu**                                  | **Any**        | Dirty Popup                   | Dirty Popup    | Dirty Popup   |
|                      | **Through Link inside screen**                    | **Any**        | No Validation, No Dirty Popup | Dirty Popup    | Validation    |

1.  **Execute:** Execute will autofire the query while rendering the page. This is set as the default value.

2.  **Fill:** If the q_saved_qur_action is marked as true then the “q_saved_qur_id” will be filled on search.

The Tree Screen Type is designed to represent hierarchical data in a structured manner. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organisational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets.

**Implementation:**

##### Data Preparation:

To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure. Here’s a sample JSON array:

[{

"key_01": "value_1",

"key_02": "value_2",

"key_03": "value_3",

"child": [{

"key_01": "value_11",

"key_02": "value_22",

"key_03": "value_33",

"child": [{

"key_01": "value_111",

"key_02": "value_222",

"key_03": "value_333",

"child": [{

"key_01": "value_1111",

"key_02": "value_2222",

"key_03": "value_3333",

}]

}]

}]

}]

**JSON Structure**

- Each object represents a node in the tree.

- The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes.

- Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship.

We will store the data in other type transnode.

- Bind the section to the other type transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data.

- To assign default permissions to any additional roles, add them to the **flv_master_grp**.

- Any group having the **flv_master_perm** permission automatically inherits all permissions, regardless of what is configured in the Entity Permissions tab.

Tool Reference :
Permission groups that are configured in DEV cannot be modified. Permissions cannot be added / removed in those permission groups. They can only be enabled & disabled. Similarly for permission groups that are assigned automatically to users based on roles also cannot be unassigned, but can be marked disabled.
But, new permission groups can be created and permission can be added to those groups by admin. Those admin created groups can be assigned to users.

Users have permission groups assigned to them, and each permission group has one or more permissions in it. So, permissions that are present in the permission groups assigned to the user are considered as the permission that user has*.*

When a CRUD operation is performed on an entity and access restriction is enabled on that operation, the system checks if the user has permission to perform that operation. If the user doesn’t have permission, the request will be rejected before executing any server side callbacks. If the user has permission, then the request will be processed further.

In the DEV landscapes the permission can be assigned via the Permission Designer screen in Page Builder & Controlled in QA / PROD system via Role Permissions screen in Security & Permissions. Explain further below in the document.

Each CRUD permission allows performing a specific operation,

1.  Read - Read permission allows the user to fire a query to that entity. This is validated on the server side.

2.  Create - Create permission provides the assigned access user to create entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side.

3.  Update - Update permission provides the assigned user access to update existing entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side.

4.  Delete - Delete permission provides the assigned user access to delete existing entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side.

5.  Download - Download permission is a template permission and doesn’t come with any validation by default. It controls the download excel button visibility in wizard created screens.

Similarly in case of online query fired from client also, the query will be rejected if sufficient permissions are not found. Incase a query from entity A inner joins entity B. The user executing the query is expected to have permissions for both entity A & entity B. Consider a modelled query belongs to entity A, and it has inner join to entity B.The cases are as follows,

1.  The user has permission to A & B - The query will be executed and the result set will be returned as usual.

2.  The user doesn’t have permission to A / B - The query will be rejected at entry point and no server side query callbacks will be executed.

3.  The user has permission to read B, but not A - The query will be rejected at entry point and no server side query callbacks will be executed.

4.  The user has permission to read A, but not B - The query will be rejected while parsing the query, but before query callback will get executed.

Middleware messages are also validated against the permission of the user who created the message. If the user who generated that message doesn’t have required permissions, the message will fail to process and will be moved to error q.

This is not applicable for CRUD operation performed inside the server. Once the request reaches the server, and is validated, any further CRUD operations performed in the rules are not validated.

Similarly for any server side triggered activities i.e. CRUD performed in the scheduler, appservices will not be restricted.

In the current Menu Builder both roles & permission can be added to a menu. But, if permission is provided, the visibility will be followed based on the permission. If not provided, it follows the old behaviour*.*

chunks.h: 4.7. What is expected ? > 4.7.4. What to expect in versioning ?
chunks.x:
Permission groups, their permissions and assigned roles can be changed in the ongoing versions. When the newer version is transported. During the transport, the permission groups & permissions in the groups of the newer version will be copied to runtime, overriding the older version configuration.

All the users who got upgraded to the new version will get permission groups assigned based on their application role and the users permissions will be adjusted based on their new permission groups.

In case of minor version deployment, where there are users who are running on older versions, Permission groups assignment will not be changed for those users. Permission adjustments will not be triggered for those users i.e. If new permissions were added to an existing group / removed from the existing group in dev, will not reflect. Permissions will be adjusted when there is a change detected in the application assignment that is relevant to permissions i.e. version upgrade, role changes, application assignment removal, admin changing assignment / permission group permissions ..etc.

**Date of Issue: 30 October 2026**

**Target Audience: Application Developers, Consultants, Trainees**

**Prepared by: Raman Kumar Gupta**

**Platform Version: 7.2.x**

*A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.*

This document helps the Application Team find the exact source of a query fired from a Procify application, optimize that query, trace the generated SQL, and use the relevant framework (FW) APIs efficiently.

Details about

- Covers: locating the query source, query optimization techniques, enabling sufficient logging to inspect the generated query, and using FW APIs (e.g. addEndpoint) optimally.

- Access to Procify Data Studio for the app/flavor under investigation.

- A working Private Node checkout of the application source (see the Private Node Setup guide).

- Access to Design Studio → Query Console (formerly SQL Executor).

- Access to Google Cloud Logging for the environment under investigation.

chunks.h: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature
chunks.x: Not Applicable — the methods in this guide (Where Used List, Network Initiator, Private Node search, query logging) are built-in platform capabilities and do not require separate enablement. The optional logging flags are listed under Configurations below and Google Cloud Logging guide.

chunks.h: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature > 3.1 How to use the feature > A. Finding the source of a query — Where Used List (Procify Data Studio)
chunks.x:
1. Open Procify Data Studio and select the App/Flavor that owns the entity or query in question.

2. In the entity/query tree, locate the Entity, Query, Property, Value Help, or Event Exit you want to trace.

3. Open the “Where Used List” option for that object. It lists every screen, query, rule, or event exit that references it, along with the property type / value help used where applicable.

4. Use this list to narrow down which module(s)/screen(s) could be responsible for firing the query, before checking Network calls or code.

chunks.h: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature > 3.1 How to use the feature > B. Finding the source of a query — Chrome Network Initiator
chunks.x:
1. Open the application in Chrome and press F12 (or right-click → Inspect) to open DevTools.

2. Switch to the Network tab, make sure recording is on, and clear existing entries for a clean trace.

3. Reproduce the action in the application so the request fires.

4. Find the relevant XHR/Fetch request (filter by “Fetch/XHR”).

5. Click the request, then open the “Initiator” tab — it shows the call stack (exact file and line) that issued the request.

6. Click any frame in the Initiator stack to jump to that source line in the Sources panel.

chunks.h: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature > 3.1 How to use the feature > C. Finding the source of a query — Private Node (Find in Folder)
chunks.x:
1. Set up / start your Private Node for the flavor in question.

2. Open the application’s source checkout in VS Code, e.g. the src folder under the flavor’s workspace.

3. In the Explorer, right-click the src folder → Find in Folder.

4. Search for the query ID / entity ID / property name. Use “Match Whole Word” to avoid false positives.

5. Review every places where this query/entity is used

chunks.h: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature > 3.1 How to use the feature > D. Optimizing the query
chunks.x:
1. Paste the query definition and surrounding code into an AI assistant (**Recommended : Claude AI with Procify Knowledge Assistant**) and ask for unnecessary joins, unused columns, and missing filters/indexes. Never paste real customer data or credentials.

2. Apply setPartialSelect([...]) to return only the needed entity properties.

3. Set setLoadAll(false) unless full-row data is genuinely required.

4. Apply setLimit(n)

6. Push filters into the query (setColumnFilter) instead of filtering in code afterward.

7. **Important**: Expand All and an INNER JOIN on the same relation are not supported together — confirm which is configured before removing either.

8. Re-run the optimized query in the Query Console and compare row counts / execution time.

   Query Console- User Guide

9. Re-run the screen end-to-end on Private Node and capture a before/after timing as evidence.

chunks.h: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature > 3.1 How to use the feature > E. Using addEndpoint and other apis efficiently
chunks.x:
| **SN** | **Steps**                                                                                                                    |

| 1      | Call addEndpoint once per Business Object, not once per child entity — it already sends the full BO tree by default.         |
| 2      | Leave onlydirtyobject at its default (true) to send only changed children; set false only when every child must be included. |
| 3      | Leave onlyRootEntity at its default (false) so children are included automatically.                                          |
| 4      | Consolidate repeated addEndpoint calls against the same BO’s children into one call.                                         |

The following flags and settings control how much query/transaction detail is captured for debugging, without needing extra code.

| **Parameter**                        | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| txn.enableStackTrace                 | Boolean on the transaction (default false). Set true to record a stack trace of all activities of the transaction, including queries executed. Switch off again once captured.                      |
| enableQueryStats                     | Framework-internal flag (default true) driving query statistics collection. Do not disable unless instructed by platform engineering.                                                               |
| "enableReqDump": true (klarion.json) | Captures full incoming request payloads into the req_dump folder. Disabled by default. Turn off again after the investigation — req_dump folders have previously grown to multiple GB when left on. |
| Select Distinct (Query → Detail)     | Set loadAll = true only when true column-level distinctness is required; otherwise leave Select Distinct off.                                                                                       |

| setPartialSelect(entityPropertyNames: string[]): KloQueryForRule |

| **Parameter**       | **Description**                                                                                |

| entityPropertyNames | Array of return-entity property IDs to select, instead of every property on the return entity. |

| setLoadAll(val: boolean): KloQueryForRule |

| **Parameter** | **Description**                                                                                                         |

| val           | Whether to load all fields of the return entity at execution time. Set false to skip properties/relations not required. |

| setLimit(limitValue: number): KloQueryForRule |

| **Parameter** | **Description**                                                                 |

| limitValue    | Maximum number of records to fetch — use for pagination on list/search screens. |

| setExpandAll(relations: string): string |

| **Parameter** | **Description**                                                                                         |

| relations     | Comma-separated relation IDs to expand. Not supported together with an INNER JOIN on the same relation. |

| addEndpoint(endpoint, type, channel, object?, onlydirtyobject?, onlyRootEntity?): EndPointBean |

| **Parameter**   | **Description**                                                                         |

| endpoint        | Endpoint ID(s) to notify — meaning depends on type (BP_USER, ENDPOINT, USER).           |
| type            | EndpointType — determines how endpoint is interpreted.                                  |
| channel         | ChannelType filter on qualifying endpoints (default DEVICE).                            |
| object          | The KloEntity whose full BO tree is sent. Defaults to the event object.                 |
| onlydirtyobject | Default true — only dirty child entities are included. Set false to force all children. |
| onlyRootEntity  | Default false — children already included. Set true to send the root entity alone.      |

*Note: A single addEndpoint call already messages the root entity and its (dirty) children — avoid a separate call per child entity.*

| getExecutedQuery(queryid, saveQueryObj, flavor?): Promise\> |

| **Parameter** | **Description**                                     |

| queryid       | Query name or entity name.                          |
| saveQueryObj  | Saved query parameters to apply.                    |
| flavor        | Optional — flavor to resolve the query/entity from. |

chunks.t: How to use Data Access Rules
chunks.x:
Users can use this action to recalculate the access tokens of an application’s entities. Multiple entities can be selected. This feature can be used to re-calculate the Data Access Keys.

| **Fields**       | **Description**                                                                  |

| **App**          | Allows users to select an app.                                                   |
| **Entity**       | Lets users select entities for recalculation. Multiple entities can be selected. |
| **All Entities** | Clicking this will select / deselect all entities for the selected app.          |

Once the recalculation is successful, the list on the screen will update, and a success message will appear: “**Recalculation done successfully!**”.

**Note** : This is a heavy process depending upon the volume of data and complexity of row wise authorization implementation. i.e. It will re-generate all the tokens which internally calls the onAccessTokenCalculate for all existing data. Avoid triggering this during active hours in Production.

1.  When using getResult / setResult on the server side for row wise authorized entities, make sure not to send back non authorized data. The data set on to the query using setResults are directly returned as query results, no more filtration is applied.

2.  When changing callback from client side to server side always consider row wise authorization if involved.

3.  Avoid logging sensitive data.

4.  Native query doesn’t support row wise authorization, so don’t select sensitive data via native query.

5.  Use “me” token only if all users of applications can access the data, else don’t use me token, use a different access key and add User Access Keys in callback.

6.  ValueHelp where row wise authorization is turned off should not have any sensitive data as key or description.

7.  The data based on which User Access Keys are generated, should be protected. **For example :** If Access to issues is based on projects assigned, then, only authorized users should be able to assign or un-assign projects.

8.  Query fired on server side will not have row wise authorization / permission applied on it. To apply row wise authorization on server side queries, use applyRowWiseAuthorization.

1.  The feature is for restricting unauthorized access. Only implement on entities with sensitive data. For non-sensitive data, consider using query filtrations.

2.  In the User Access Keys callback, make sure to batch queries based on user, as it can be called for 1 - many users.

Row wise authorization is a security feature provided by a framework with which access to entity data can be restricted to selective row items on user level. By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens.
*Basics of BOL features.*
*By default row wise authorization is disabled in all entities, it can be enabled in Data Studio.*

How does Row-wise authorization work ?

Row wise authorization works by filtering records on the server level by matching tokens (strings that are used to create a mapping) between user and data.

A simple illustration like:

**Entity Data:**

data1 -> [token1, token2]

data2 -> [token2, token3]

data3 -> [token4, token5]

**User tokens:**

user1 -> [token1] -> [data1]

user2 -> [token1, token2] -> [data1, data2]

user3 -> [token3, token4] -> [data2, data3]

user4 -> [] -> []

Consider an entity ENT_A, where row wise authorization is enabled, and each record in ENT_A has a set of tokens assigned to it. Consider user USER_A, who has a set of tokens for that entity assigned to him. When USER_A fires a query, he will get only the records in the entity ENT_A which have at least of the tokens that USER_A has.

Access token is a string, which acts as a link between the data and user to define which data set the user has access to. Consider the above example. There are access tokens for each record of data (Data Access Keys), and below that there is a set of access token(s) assigned to each user (User Access Keys).

Row wise authorization can be enabled only in root entities. Not on child entities. If BO is row wise authorized, all the child entities will also follow the same authorization.

chunks.h: 4.13. Value help behavior with ROW wise authentication
chunks.x: An entity is secured with **row-wise authorization**, meaning users can only see rows assigned or accessible to them. However, there are cases where users may need to see **all rows** in the value help suggestion items. This requirement is addressed with the **"Ignore Row-wise Auth"** toggle.

chunks.h: 4.13. Value help behavior with ROW wise authentication > Key Highlights:
chunks.x:
- **Ignore Row-wise Auth toggle** allows users to **view all rows** in the value help suggestions.

- This **does not completely bypass authorization**; only properties used in the value help are visible.

- Other properties will be **undefined or null**, ensuring sensitive data remains protected.

- **Sensitive properties involved in row-wise authorization should NOT be included** in the value help when this toggle is enabled.

chunks.h: 4.13. Value help behavior with ROW wise authentication > How It Works:
chunks.x:
- Enabling **row-wise authorization** automatically assigns a **query to the value help (VH)**.

- This query is applied across **all value helps in the entity** that have the "Ignore Row-wise Auth" toggle enabled.

- When the **toggle is disabled**, the query is removed.

  - Users must then **assign their own query or entity** to the value help.

  - In this mode, **only authorized rows are visible** in the suggestion items.

chunks.h: 4.14. Server side behaviour of queries to row wise authorized entities > 4.14.1. Applying Row-wise Authorization in Server-side Queries
chunks.x:
By default, when a query is executed from server-side logic—such as Create/Update/Delete rules, schedulers, app service logic, or beforeQuery / afterQuery callbacks—it does not apply row-wise authorization automatically.

To enable row-wise filters in such cases, use the following API available on the **KloQuery** or **KloQueryForRule** instance:

| applyRowWiseAuthorization(userIdToImpersonate?: string): Promise\ |

chunks.h: 4.14. Server side behaviour of queries to row wise authorized entities > 4.14.2. Usage Details:
chunks.x:
- **userIdToImpersonate (optional)**:
  > Pass the user ID whose row-level access you want to apply.

  - If not provided, it will default to **\$SYSTEM.userID**.

In the past, the framework has provided the application with screen lifecycle events like onScreenEnter, onModelCreate, onTranscationEnter, onAfterTransactionEnter, onTranscationExit, onModelDestroy, and onScreenExit. But in the applications which run with version 6.0 or higher, the above-mentioned events are removed and new events have been introduced.

- onPageInit

- onPageModelReady

- onPageEnter

- onPageExit

- onPageDestroy

1.  onPageInit

    1.  This event will be called as soon as the controller is loaded. The transaction, model and UI are yet to be created for this controller when this event is called.

    2.  This event will be called only once.

2.  onPageModelReady

    1.  This event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the Data is not set to the model yet. From this event, the developer can call the skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then he/she should be responsible for setting the data in the model.

    2.  This event will also be called once.

3.  onPageEnter

    1.  This event will be called whenever the screen enters the visible area using navigation (Both front and back navigation). If the navigation is within the same screen, this event will not be triggered.

    2.  This event will be called after the data is set(if the model preparation is not skipped) to the model.

4.  onPageExit

    1.  This event will be called in the source screen whenever the developer navigates to a different screen.

    2.  The developer can call cancelNavigation API which will cancel the navigation.

5.  onPageDestroy

    1.  This event is called when the screen is destroyed. Destruction of the screen is initiated only during back navigation.

2.  This event will be called only once.

All the events hold a read-only object as a parameter which holds information such as if the screen is initialized or not, if the navigation to the screen is from an external source or not, navigation parameters and source screen ID from where the navigation is triggered.

Below code snippet, imports pdf-lib and generates the pdf , convert to blob object and uploads it via setAttachmentP API   // Import pdf-lib for server-side PDF generation         const { PDFDocument, rgb } \= require("pdf-lib");         // Create a new PDF document         const pdfDoc \= await PDFDocument.create();         const page \= pdfDoc.addPage([595, 842]);         // Add content to the PDF         page.drawText("ORDER DOCUMENT", {             x: 50,             y: 800,             size: 18,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         page.drawText("=".repeat(80), {             x: 50,             y: 780,             size: 8,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         page.drawText(`Order ID: \${this.order_id || "N/A"}`, {             x: 50,             y: 750,             size: 12,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         page.drawText(`Order Description: \${this.order_desc || "N/A"}`, {             x: 50,             y: 730,             size: 12,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         page.drawText(`Created Date: \${new Date().toLocaleDateString()}`, {             x: 50,             y: 700,             size: 12,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         page.drawText(`Created Time: \${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}`, {             x: 50,             y: 680,             size: 12,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         // Save the PDF to bytes         const pdfBytes \= await pdfDoc.save();         // Create a Blob object from PDF bytes (required by setAttachmentP)         const blob \= new Blob([pdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" });         // Set file name         const fileName \= `order_\${this.order_id || "new"}_\${Date.now()}.pdf`;         // Upload the PDF using setAttachmentP         await this.attach.setAttachmentP(blob, fileName);*  |
