chunks.x: | 1 | *From the server side callback function, We can retrieve the previously generated PDF reports and modify them. Below code snippet, that retrieves the pdf, modified it and uploads it via setAttachmentP API  // Import pdf-lib for server-side PDF modification         const { PDFDocument, rgb } \= require("pdf-lib");         // Load the existing attachment from server (returns Uint8Array)         const existingAttachment \= await this.attach.getAttachmentServerLoadP();         if (!existingAttachment) {             throw new Error("No attachment found to update");         }         // Load the existing PDF document directly from Uint8Array         const pdfDoc \= await PDFDocument.load(existingAttachment);         // Get the first page (or add a new page if needed)         const pages \= pdfDoc.getPages();         const firstPage \= pages[0];         // Add updated/modified content to the PDF         firstPage.drawText("*** UPDATED ***", {             x: 50,             y: 650,             size: 14,             color: rgb(1, 0, 0), // Red color to indicate update         });         firstPage.drawText(`Last Modified: \${new Date().toLocaleString()}`, {             x: 50,             y: 630,             size: 12,             color: rgb(0, 0, 1), // Blue color         });         firstPage.drawText(`Modified Order Description: \${this.order_desc || "N/A"} - MODIFIED`, {             x: 50,             y: 610,             size: 12,             color: rgb(0, 0, 0),         });         // Save the modified PDF to bytes         const modifiedPdfBytes \= await pdfDoc.save();         // Create a Blob object from modified PDF bytes         const modifiedBlob \= new Blob([modifiedPdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" });         // Generate updated file name         const updatedFileName \= `order_\${this.order_id || "new"}_updated_\${Date.now()}.pdf`;         // Upload the modified PDF using setAttachmentP         await this.attach.setAttachmentP(modifiedBlob, updatedFileName);*  |

chunks.h: Server Side Attachment Upload — API Details
chunks.x:
| API Name | setAttachmentP of attachment qualifier |

| **Parameter 1** | *File Blob* |
| **Parameter 2** | File name |
|  |  |
| **Parameter** | **Description** |
| *File Blob* |  *blob object of the attachment that needs to be uploaded*  |
| file_name | Name of the file with extension Example: report.pdf |

The following BOL API methods are available on any entity property with the attachment qualifier. In server-side callbacks they are called on the property through this, for example this.attach where attach is the property name.

setAttachmentP(fileBlob, fileName): Promise\

**fileBlob** (Blob): Blob object of the attachment to upload.

**fileName** (string): Name of the file, including the extension. Example: report.pdf

Promise\: resolves once the file is uploaded to the attachment property.

Uploads a file to the attachment qualifier property. It supports uploads from both server side and client side. On the server side, generate the report (PDF, CSV and so on), convert it to a Blob object and pass it to this method.

const pdfBytes \= await pdfDoc.save();
const blob \= new Blob([pdfBytes], { type: "application/pdf" });
const fileName \= `order_\${this.order_id || "new"}_\${Date.now()}.pdf`;
await this.attach.setAttachmentP(blob, fileName);

getAttachmentServerLoadP(): Promise\

Promise\: content of the file currently stored in the attachment property. The value is empty when no attachment exists.

Loads the existing attachment from the server so that it can be read or modified in a server-side callback. To save the changes, upload the modified file again with setAttachmentP.

**Date of Issue: 28/03/2024**

**Version: 7.0
Target Audience: Developers**

- The System should have Chrome installed.

- Access to the required HTTP port number, host address and UUID for debugging.

- For Server Debugging in the server, a ticket needs to be raised to the Infra team in Jira with the below information in the case of local/AWS servers.

  - Reason for debugging and ticket no of the issue if exists.

  - Timeline for debugging.

- In the case of customer servers, send a mail to the customer team to enable the http debugging port in the firewall.

- After providing the above information, approval from Piyush is required in the case of local/AWS servers.

- Once Approval is provided, the Infra will provide the access to debugging http port i.e. opening the http debugging port in the firewall in case of local/aws servers and the Customer team will allow the port for customer servers after taking the necessary approvals from their teams.

  - Infra Team → AWS servers

  - Infra Team → Local Servers

  - Customer Team → Customer servers

**Note:** AWS DEV Server debugging is possible only within the Jump server(AWS).

**Step 1:** Start the landscape-specific Bol Node server with the below command: **[Take the help of the Infra Team to start the BOL Node]**

F:\Klarion 6.0\BOL_NODE> node **--inspect=0.0.0.0:9229** **--max-old-space-size=2048** --unhandled-rejections=none closedmodules/kloBolServer_6-0/kloIDE/kloBolServerIndex.js **servingLandscapes=APPS**

Details are given below:

| **Elements**                                                   | **Descriptions**                                    |

| **F:\Klarion 6.0\BOL_NODE**                                    | This is the Bolnode path (public node path).        |
| **--inspect=0.0.0.0:9229**       | This port 9229 for remote debugging.                |
| **--max-old-space-size**                                       | This is used for specifying the heap size.          |
| **closedmodules/kloBolServer_6-0/kloIDE/kloBolServerIndex.js** | the entry point to the node application to start.   |
| **servingLandscapes=APPS (APPS – Landscape Name )**            | provide the landscape name which you need to debug. |

- When the --inspect switch is put, a Node.js process looks for a debugging client. By default, it will look at the host and port 127.0.0.1:9229. Each process is also assigned a unique UUID.

- Inspector clients must know and specify the **host address**, **port number**, and **UUID** to connect.

> A full URL will look something like:
>
> ws://127.0.0.1:9229/0f2c936f-b1cd-4ac9-aab3-f63b0f33d55e

- If the debugger is bound to a public IP address, or 0.0.0.0, any clients that can reach your IP address will be able to connect to the debugger without any restriction and will be able to run arbitrary codes.

**Note:** By default, node --inspect binds to 127.0.0.1. You explicitly need to provide a public IP address or 0.0.0.0, etc., if you intend to allow external connections to the debugger.

Once the server is started with the above configurations mentioned, then connect to the system and open Chrome & follow the below instructions for debugging the BOLNODE server.

**Step 3:** In the Chrome search bar, type “**chrome://inspect**”

>

**Step 4:** In DevTools > Devices select “**Open dedicated DevTools For Node**”

>

**Step 5:** In the new tab that will be opened in a new window, select “**Add Connection**”.

>

**Step 6:** We will put the **Server** **IP address** and the **Debugging** **Port No.** in the Network address field and **Add** the same.

>

**Step 7:** Refresh the page once more to find the target node.

API name: createTable

Method: GET

There are four levels of schema update, the parameters guide for each level type is mentioned below:

> This is for updating all the tables of one/multiple flavors.
>
> Mandatory Parameters: **update_level**, **landscape**, **fv_list**, **consider**
>
> Optional params: **log_required**, **force_uncompatible, is_config**
>
> **{**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **update_level: "flavor",**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **consider: "table",/* "table" or "index" */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], /* multiple flavors are also allowed but the sequence has to be maintained properly (parent,child)*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **log_required: false,/* true or false*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **force_uncompatible: false,/* true or false*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **is_config: false,/* true or false. If true, then it considers config entities(Metadata DB) */**
>
> **}**

> This is for updating the table of only one entity.
>
> Mandatory Parameters: **update_level**, **landscape**, **fv_list**, **entity_name**
>
> Optional params: **log_required**, **force_uncompatible, give_diff, is_config**
>
> **{**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **update_level: "entity",**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **entity_name: "d_no_header",/* entity name */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **consider: "table",/* table or index*/**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], /* pass only one belonging flavor in the array */**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **log_required: "FALSE",/* "TRUE" or "FALSE" */**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **force_uncompatible: false,/* true or false*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **give_diff: false,/* true or false- This will return the difference between metadata and table in DB*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **is_config: false,/* true or false- This flag indicates whether the selected entity is config or not*/**
>
> **}**

> This is for updating only one index in the table.
>
> Mandatory Parameters: **update_level**, **landscape**, **fv_list**, **index_name**
>
> Optional params: **log_required**
>
> **{**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **update_level: "index",**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **index_name: "index123",/* index id */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **consider: "index",**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **fv_list: [{fl:'eam',ver:'1'}], /* pass only one belonging flavor in the array */**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **log_required: false,/* true or false*/**
>
> **}**

> This is for updating all the tables of a landscape.
>
> Mandatory Parameters: **update_level**, **landscape**, **consider**
>
> Optional params: **log_required**, **force_uncompatible**, **drop_extra, is_config**
>
> **{**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **update_level: "landscape",**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **landscape: "tools_dev6",/* Landscape ID */**
>
> **//@mandatory**
>
> **consider: "table",/* "table" or "index" */**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **log_required: false,/* true or false*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **force_uncompatible: false,/* true or false*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **drop_extra: false/* true or false*/**
>
> **//@optional**
>
> **is_config: false,/* true or false. If true, then it considers config entities(Metadata DB) */**
>
> **}**

1.  **Table** and **Index** can not be processed at a time. The **‘consider’** flag has to be either **‘table’** or **‘index’**.

2.  For dropping additional tables and columns which are not used, createTable api has to be called at the **landscape level** and the **drop_extra** flag has to be **‘TRUE’**. API doesn't delete the tables/columns, it only **returns the deleted SQL statements**.

3.  **force_uncompatible** flag is for updating the column **domain/length** forcefully. It may result in **data truncation**. Use it wisely.

4.  The primary key change is allowed only in owning flavor.

5.  Domain, length, and precision change are not allowed in non-owning flavors.

6.  Entity scp (Scope/Persists on) needs to be maintained for creating table in server as well as in the client. If the scp is marked **both** it will create table in client and server side. scp marked as **client-only**, will create a table in client and scp **server-only** will create a table in server DB.

> **After changing the scp of the entity for server-side the changes will reflect no build will be required but in client to reflect the changes build is required.**

7.  Compatible changes are mentioned in the sheet, this list may change in future if required

Upgrade and Transport application is used to EXPORT metadata of any application version and IMPORT onto any other application version. It also helps in merging two apps' metadata into one.

App inheritance is another powerful feature which is a part of this application, that allows users to manage the application hierarchy. Read more about App Dependencies here

chunks.t: Navigate to apps in Upgrade & Transport
chunks.x:
To find the apps follow the steps below:

**Step 1:** In the portal click on the **App Lifecycle** menu header.

**Step 2:** There are four apps we’ll be using for Upgrade & Transport under **App Lifecycle**.

Export App will download metadata of any given app version(eg. Myapp 6-0-1) in the form of a zip. The exported metadata zip file can now be uploaded/imported to any other application (eg. yourapp 6-0-4).

The metadata contains all of your developments like screens, entities, menu homepage etc. (except the files like controllers, util, entity file, query file etc.)

Fill in the input fields on the Export App Page and then click on the Export button. Suppose we have an app, **5-moast4_ui-1**; then the following will be the details:
1. **Account ID: 5**

2. **Flavor ID: moast4_ui**

3. **Version ID: 1
**After this wait for a pop-up that indicates download has started.

Import App can be used to upload/import any application metadata from any server/system of Procify. Refer to export sections.

To import an app the following inputs are mandatory.

1.  **Upload Export zip:** Exported zip with the correct name like 5-flavor_name-1.zip.

2.  **Importing Account:** Account-id.

3.  **Importing App:** App with a version like app_name-1.

After filling out all fields click on import and then wait for a response we can also check the status of importing data by clicking on the check status button to ensure the task is completed or not.

App compare allows you to compare two Apps metadata(eg. Screens, entities. etc..) and pick/merge what you want from App1 and App2 then generate a 3rd App. The output of the App comparison is a new zip of metadata which can be imported to any app and that will have all screens, entities etc.. chosen in app comparison.

To compare any two applications, export metadata of the apps using Export App and upload them on the compare screens SET1 and SET2 click on compare. System will display what objects are contained in SET1(App1) and SET2(App2)

To compare among two app versions, the compare screen requires two sets of exported **app zip files** as input. After comparison, the screen gives an object-wise difference. The following difference status is shown on the screen.

1.  Only in set-1

2.  Only in set-2

3.  Same (matches in both)

4.  Different

After comparison, one can change the metadata and merge it into one app, then download the merged zip.

The Downloaded merge zip can be imported into the **Import App page** to get the merged metadata in the application.

App Dependencies is an Admin Tool that helps in managing the hierarchy of the applications.

App Inheritance is another cool feature of the procify which helps to improve the productivity and integrity of the application by packaging the development into relevant screens and objects and then using Inheritance which works similarly to object-oriented inheritance.

This tool manages the inheritance and sequence of the applications used or inherited.

The App Dependencies screen has different sections

**Apps List**: This section of the editor will list all the apps available in the landscape along with their version.

**App Detail:** The details of the selected app from the app list will be displayed in this section.

**Versions:** The versions table will list all the available versions of the selected app.

For creating a new app use the Workspace Hub application.

| **Column Header** | **Description**                                |

| App               | app name in fvid( aid_appName_version) format. |
| Version           | version of the app.                            |
| Network Mode      | App mode/network mode of that app version.     |
| Apply Changes     | Refer to the below section.                    |

Apply change can be used to cleanup duplicate metadata from child App/ inheriting app

Use the Workspace Hub application for new version creation.

The used Apps/Inherited Apps(Parent app) of the selected app version will be listed here.

| **Column Header** | **Description**                                                   |

| Used Fv’s         | App name in FVid format                                           |
| Sequence          | Sequence of the used FVs based on which the app will be inherited |

**Step 1:** Click on the application (these will be child applications) from the apps list you want to inherit from another application (you inherit from the parent app).

**Step 2:** Click on the **edit** button which is placed in the right corner of the screen.

**Step 3:** Under the **Used FVs** section, click on the **Plus(+)** button.

It will show a list of applications to select from.

**Step 4:** Choose the parent application that you want to inherit from the list. Now, it will show in the **Used FVs** section.

**Step 5:** Click on the **Save** button in the right corner of the screen.

**Step 6:** After completing **Save,** click on the **Generate App Sequence** button to update the sequence for inherited apps.

The process will be complete.

Now **Publish** the child application from the Workspace Hub.

A notification is a message, email, icon, or another symbol that appears when an application wants you to pay attention. Notifications are a way to alert you on the various important facts that have happened in your application that are worth your attention while you are not using the application.

In the UWL (Universal Work List) notification screen, if the Workflow contains user tasks, those tasks will be shown on the screen. It mainly has 2 screens, **Approver** and **Requester**.

- The approver (**Pending Approvals**) can see and take necessary actions (those actions are defined in the workflow during design time) by reviewing the tasks.

- In the Requester (**My Submissions**) screen, whatever tasks have been created or assigned will reflect, and the users can see the update of the task on this screen.

The Approver can see the requests/tasks and decide on the necessary actions to be taken for the tasks accordingly. The Requester, on the other hand, can see the updates or actions taken on the tasks or requests.

For Example: If a requester applies for a leave give the reason for the leave and the duration of the leave. Whoever is the approver for the request will see the request verify the reason and take necessary actions (like Approved or Rejected). The same way the UWL screen works but it can have different workflows.

A Workflow is defined as a sequence of tasks that processes a set of data through a specific path from initiation to completion. It helps users to manage business processes efficiently.

Workflows are useful for processes that include several people, a sequence of tasks and coordination between different objects.

This is a tool which allows users to create workflows for entities of a particular app, which get executed during runtime based on the action taken on the entity i.e. Create/Update/Delete.

To perform a complex business process such as ‘Employee Onboarding’, involves going through different steps. Users can define those steps in the workflow in the form of tasks and manage the sequence by connecting them.
For automation of complex workflows within the organisation.

**SCHEDULE Event:** Task_onDeadline, Task_onEscalation, Task_onReminder

Schedule events can be added in User Task, if deadline,reminder,escalation are provided. On occurrence of these events through the scheduler, expression evaluation and assignment occurs based on process data provided.

**Important:** There are a few things we need to know about App Versioning. The App versions are written in 6-0-1(Major-Minor-Patch).

Here, 6 is referred to as Major

0 is referred to as Minor and,

1 is referred to as Patch

* When the patch is changed while versioning, the **roles & users** are automatically copied from the previous version to the recent version.

chunks.t: FW Version Maintenance for Parent and Child Applications
chunks.h: Workspace Hub — FW Version Maintenance for Parent and Child Applications
chunks.x:
1. All flavors within a single application hierarchy must use the same FW version to ensure compatibility and consistency.
2. If any application in the hierarchy (that has dependencies with other flavors) requires a FW version upgrade, **all associated flavors within that hierarchy must also be updated to the same new FW version**.

**Example:**

 If `em4_6-0-1` plans to upgrade to a newer FW version (e.g., `6-1-0`), then every other flavor under the same hierarchy must be versioned accordingly and updated to use `6-1-0`.
 However, independent flavors that do not belong to this hierarchy are not required to update their FW version.

kloBroker is a broker between tenants, clients, and external systems. It enables communication via messaging and queues. kloBroker runs on the master node in the kloSystem. There can be multiple instances, one per kloLandscape.

This dialog allows the user to modify klobroker fields such as mw_msg_pick, mw required, notif required, bol enabled, fcm server key, base path, external file size, holding time, notif interval, notif threshold, interval, queue size, threshold, queue creation class, max message per file, SQL batch size, notif pick size and file parallel count.

This dialog also allows CRUD on klobroker external fields which contain endpointid, type, destination host, destination port, destination protocol, user ID, password, and destination path.

Description for the above fields are as follows:

| **Fields**         | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| MW Msg Pick        | This implies the number of messages middleware can pick from the tenant_q table.                                                                                                                    |
| MW Required        | This implies whether middleware is required or not.                                                                                                                                                 |
| Notif Required     | Server will send push notifications to the device. It will push all notifications to one table(ma_notification_queue).                                                                              |
| FCM Server Key     | To sync the message from the server to the device, fcm_server_key is mandatory.                                                                                                                     |
| Base Path          | SAP will put files in this folder and the server will pick files.                                                                                                                                   |
| External File Size | Size of the external files                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Notif Interval     | It will check in the queue at intervals whether the

messages are present or not.                                                                                                                    |
| Notif threshold    | The Maximum number of notifications the server will pick.                                                                                                                                           |
| Interval           | For how much time the DB needs to be checked, the Server will check whether the file is available or not in the sap in the folder and if the file is available then it will process or it will not. |
| Threshold          | The number of messages the server will hold at a time.                                                                                                                                              |
| Notif pick size    | The number of notifications it can pick at a time                                                                                                                                                   |

This will only consider **SAP_LOCAL** or **SAP_ONLINE**. It will not consider if it has any extra symbols or any extensions like **SAP_LOCAL_** or **SAP_LOCAL**.

Description for the above fields are as follows:

| **Fields**       | **Description**                                                                                                                               |

| SAP_LOCAL        | If something is being saved in the DB, then it will go to tenant_q and save in the klarion db, then we need to push to SAP as a JSON message. |
| SAP_ONLINE       | When we are directly accessing the SAP server without saving in our db, in this case, we use SAP_ONLINE.                                      |
| TYPE             |                                                                                                                                               |
| Destination Host | Here we are maintaining the url provided by SAP.                                                                                              |
| User Id          | User Id provided by SAP for the url.                                                                                                          |
| Password         | Password provided by SAP for the url.                                                                                                         |
| Destination Path | When the type is a folder, then we specify a path here.                                                                                       |

Application configuration wizard is to create a new application in the system by taking the necessary information, an application can also be created by taking a reference of an existing application.

- All configuration tables in the system.

- The Application wizard and its components in the system.

chunks.h: Workspace Settings — Configs > 1.15. Sap Config > 1.15.1 Application creation Wizard > 1.15.1.3.Process Flow
chunks.x:
**Path** : Wizards → Application Wizard

**Tcode** : /MVN/APP_WIZARD

**Report** : /MVN/RP_APP_WIZARD

Execute the **Tcode** or use **Menu** to open the wizard. It enters the start page of the wizard as shown below.

##### **Wizard steps**

- Please read the guidelines provided in each step of the wizard carefully before proceeding with the execution of that step.

##### **Name and Integration parameters**

- This step is for setting up the application configuration.

| **Input**           | **Purpose**                                                                      | **Possible values**           |

| Application-Version | App and version of the newly created app.                                        | Eg:eam-1                      |
| Integration Mode    | Integration mode of app                                                          | Online/ Offline               |
| Integration Type    | Integration type of app                                                          | File/Gateway/PI or PO         |
| Reference From      | All Informations will be copied from the reference app to the newly creating app | Existing App name and version |

- Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step.

##### **Connection parameter**

- This step is to provide the Connection parameters of the application.

chunks.h: Workspace Settings — Configs > 1.15. Sap Config > 1.15.1 Application creation Wizard > 1.15.1.3.Process Flow
chunks.x:
| **Input**       | **Purpose**          | **Possible values** |

| Gateway/PI URL  | URL of gateway or PI |                     |
| Gateway RFC     | Gateway RFC name     |                     |
| Inbound folder  | Inbound folder path  |                     |
| Outbound folder | Outbound folder path |                     |

- Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step.

##### **Token parameter**

- This step is to configure the token parameter of the application for the provided gateway information.

| **Input**           | **Purpose**                 | **Possible values** |

| Token URL           | Token url                   |                     |
| Username            | User name of the URL access |                     |
| Password            | Password of the URL access  |                     |
| SSL ID              | SSL ID of the connection    |                     |
| Proxy               | Proxy                       |                     |
| RFC: Gateway to SAP | Gateway to SAP RFC          |                     |

- Once all token parameters are provided, click the ‘TEST’ icon to verify the connection.

- This will display the connection status as shown below.

- Click on continue to move to the next step.

##### **Middleware parameter**

chunks.h: Workspace Settings — Configs > 1.15. Sap Config > 1.15.1 Application creation Wizard > 1.15.1.3.Process Flow
chunks.x:
- Modify the default middleware parameter values in this step according to the requirements, then click continue to proceed to the next page.

- Click the ‘Del’ icon in the table to remove parameters.

##### **Message parameter**

- Edit the default message parameters in this step based on the requirement and click on continue to move on to the next page.

##### **Copy other configurations**

- This step involves selecting the configurations to be copied to the new app if a reference app is available.

| **Input**             | **Purpose**                                      | **Possible Values** |

| Profile determination | To copy the profile determination configurations |                     |
| BO Handler            | To copy the BO Handler configurations            |                     |
| Klo Model             | To copy the Klo Model configurations             |                     |
| F4 Mappings           | To copy the F4 Mappings configurations           |                     |

- Select the checkbox if the specified configurations should be copied.

- This applies only if a reference app is provided in the Name and Integration parameters section.

##### **Wizard Finish**

- Review the provided details in the wizard summary and click the Complete button to finalize the application creation.
